काश्यपेयोऽमृतो ज्ञेयो नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः ॥
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो देवशत्रुनिषूदनः ॥ 50 ॥
4.186.m: son of Kaśyapa, known as immortal, enemy of serpents, vehicle of Viṣṇu, / immeasurable, invincible, slayer of the gods' enemies,

4.186.s:
garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ ..
śastravarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣāsmāṃśca ripūndaha .. 51 .. .. (iti dhvajamaṃtraḥ) .. ..
4.186.d:
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः ॥
शस्त्रवर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्मांश्च रिपून्दह ॥ 51 ॥ ॥ (इति ध्वजमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.186.m: Garuḍa, swift as the wind, stands close at hand within you. / Protect our weapons, armour, arms, and warriors, and burn our enemies!' (Thus the banner mantra.)

4.186.s:
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadaṃto'tha vāmanaḥ ..
supratīkoñjano nīla ete'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ .... 52 ..
4.186.d:
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदंतोऽथ वामनः ॥
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नील एतेऽष्टौ देवयोनयः ॥॥ 52 ॥
4.186.m: 'Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are of divine origin;

4.186.s:
eteṣāṃ putrapautrāśca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ ..
bhadro mandro mṛgaścaiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca ..
vanevane prasūtāste kariyoniṃ mahāgajāḥ..53..
4.186.d:
एतेषां पुत्रपौत्राश्च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः ॥
भद्रो मन्द्रो मृगश्चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च ॥
वनेवने प्रसूतास्ते करियोनिं महागजाः॥53॥
4.186.m: and their sons and grandsons have resorted to eight armies. / Bhadra, Mandra, Mṛga, and Saṃkīrṇa elephants— / those great elephants born in every forest have attained the elephant species.

4.186.s:
pātu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ ..
bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaṃ pratipālayan .. 54 ..
4.186.d:
पातु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः ॥
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयं प्रतिपालयन् ॥ 54 ॥
4.186.m: May the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas along with the hosts of Maruts protect you! / Protect your master, O lord of elephants, keeping your covenant!

4.186.s:
avāpurhi jayaṃ yuddhe gamane svasti no vraja ..
śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavonilāt ..
sthairyaṃ merorjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devātpuraṃdarāt .. 55 ..
4.186.d:
अवापुर्हि जयं युद्धे गमने स्वस्ति नो व्रज ॥
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवोनिलात् ॥
स्थैर्यं मेरोर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात्पुरंदरात् ॥ 55 ॥
4.186.m: They indeed attained victory in battle; advance for our well-being on the march! / May your splendour come from Soma, strength from Viṣṇu, radiance from the Sun, speed from the Wind,

4.186.s:
yuddhe rakṣaṃtu nāgāstvāṃ diśaśca saha daivataiḥ ..
aśvinau saha gaṃdharvaiḥ pāṃtu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā .. 56 .. ( iti hastimaṃtraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
युद्धे रक्षंतु नागास्त्वां दिशश्च सह दैवतैः ॥
अश्विनौ सह गंधर्वैः पांतु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥ 56 ॥ ( इति हस्तिमंत्रः ॥)
4.186.m: steadfastness from Meru, victory from Rudra, and glory from the god Indra! / In battle may the serpents protect you, and the directions along with the deities; / may the Aśvins along with the Gandharvas protect you everywhere, always!' (Thus the elephant mantra.)

4.186.s:
hutabhugvasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ ..
nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣa bhūtagaṇāgrahāḥ .. 57 ..
4.186.d:
हुतभुग्वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः ॥
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्ष भूतगणाग्रहाः ॥ 57 ॥
4.186.m: 'The Fire-god, Vasus, Rudras, Wind, Soma, and the great sages, / the hosts of serpents, Kinnaras, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and ghosts, and the planets,

4.186.s:
pramathāśca sahādityairbhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha ..
śakrasenāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritāstvayi .. 58 ..
4.186.d:
प्रमथाश्च सहादित्यैर्भूतेशो मातृभिः सह ॥
शक्रसेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितास्त्वयि ॥ 58 ॥
4.186.m: the Pramathas along with the Ādityas, the Lord of ghosts along with the Mothers, / Skanda the commander of Indra's army, and Varuṇa are situated in you.

4.186.s:
pradahaṃtu ripūnsarvānrājā vijayamṛcchatu ..
yāni prayuktānyaribhirdūṣaṇāni samaṃtataḥ .. 59 ..
4.186.d:
प्रदहंतु रिपून्सर्वान्राजा विजयमृच्छतु ॥
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्दूषणानि समंततः ॥ 59 ॥
4.186.m: May they burn all enemies; may the king attain victory! / Whatever harms have been employed on every side by the foes,

4.186.s:
etāni paraśatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā ..
kālanemivadhe yuddhe yuddhe tripuraghātane .. 60 ..
4.186.d:
एतानि परशत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा ॥
कालनेमिवधे युद्धे युद्धे त्रिपुरघातने ॥ 60 ॥
4.186.m: may these of the external enemies be destroyed by your splendour! / In the battle for the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle for the destruction of Tripura,

4.186.s:
hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe yuddhe devāsure tathā ..
śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhamānāstu bhūpateḥ .. 61 ..
4.186.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे युद्धे देवासुरे तथा ॥
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभमानास्तु भूपतेः ॥ 61 ॥
4.186.m: in the battle with Hiraṇyakaśipu, and likewise in the war between the gods and asuras, / you shone; even so, today, shine for the king!

4.186.s:
nīlāṃ śvetāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā naśyaṃtvadya nṛpārayaḥ ..
vyādhibhirvividhairghoraiḥ śastraiśca yudhi nirjitāḥ .. 62 ..
4.186.d:
नीलां श्वेतामिमां दृष्ट्वा नश्यंत्वद्य नृपारयः ॥
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर्घोरैः शस्त्रैश्च युधि निर्जिताः ॥ 62 ॥
4.186.m: Having seen this dark and white [standard], may the king's enemies perish today, / vanquished in battle by terrible, manifold diseases and by weapons!

4.186.s: sadyaḥ svasthā bhavaṃti sma tvadvātenāpamārjitāḥ .. 63 ..
4.186.d: सद्यः स्वस्था भवंति स्म त्वद्वातेनापमार्जिताः ॥ 63 ॥
4.186.m: They became well at once, swept over by your breeze. 63.

4.186.s:
pūtanā revatī nāmnā kālarātrīti yā smṛtā ..
dahaṃtvāśu ripūnsarvānpatāke tvāmupāgatāḥ .. 64 .. (iti patākāmantraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
पूतना रेवती नाम्ना कालरात्रीति या स्मृता ॥
दहंत्वाशु रिपून्सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपागताः ॥ 64 ॥ (इति पताकामन्त्रः ॥)
4.186.m: Pūtanā, Revatī by name, and she who is remembered as Kālarātrī— / having approached you, O standard, may they swiftly burn all enemies!' (Thus the standard mantra.)

4.186.s:
asiśca ripuhā khaḍgastīkṣṇakarmā durāsadaḥ ..
śrīgarbho vijayaścaiva dharmadhārastathaiva ca .. 69 ..
4.186.d:
असिश्च रिपुहा खड्गस्तीक्ष्णकर्मा दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मधारस्तथैव च ॥ 69 ॥
4.186.m: 'You are the blade, the slayer of enemies, the sword, sharp in deed, hard to approach, / the womb of fortune, victory, and the bearer of righteousness.

4.186.s:
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni svayamuktāni vedhasā ..
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ .. 66 ..
4.186.d:
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि स्वयमुक्तानि वेधसा ॥
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः ॥ 66 ॥
4.186.m: Thus these eight names of yours were spoken by the Creator Himself. / Your constellation is Kṛttikā, your preceptor the god Maheśvara;

4.186.s:
hiraṇyaṃ ca śarīraṃte dhātā devojanārdanaḥ ..
pitā pitāmaho devastvaṃ māṃ pālaya sarvadā .. 67 .. (iti khaḍgamantraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
हिरण्यं च शरीरंते धाता देवोजनार्दनः ॥
पिता पितामहो देवस्त्वं मां पालय सर्वदा ॥ 67 ॥ (इति खड्गमन्त्रः ॥)
4.186.m: gold is your body, and your ordainer is the god Janārdana; / you are father and grandfather, a deity; protect me always!' (Thus the sword mantra.)

4.186.s:
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varma sarvāyaso hyasi ..
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo'haṃ tava varmannamo'stu te .. 68 .. ( iti varmamantraḥ ..) ..
4.186.d:
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्म सर्वायसो ह्यसि ॥
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयोऽहं तव वर्मन्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 68 ॥ ( इति वर्ममन्त्रः ॥) ॥
4.186.m: 'You are the granter of well-being in battle, armour entirely made of iron; / protect me, for I am to be protected by you; O armour, salutations to you!' (Thus the armour mantra.)

4.186.s:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ .ghoṣāddhṛdayakampan ..
bhava bhūmipa sainyānāṃ tathā vijayavarddhanaḥ .. 69 ..
4.186.d:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां ।घोषाद्धृदयकम्पन् ॥
भव भूमिप सैन्यानां तथा विजयवर्द्धनः ॥ 69 ॥
4.186.m: O war drum, by your sound you make the hearts of adversaries tremble; / likewise, be the enhancer of victory for the armies of the king.

4.186.s:
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyaṃti varavāraṇāḥ ..
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo'smākaṃ mudāvahaḥ ..70..
4.186.d:
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यंति वरवारणाः ॥
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षोऽस्माकं मुदावहः ॥70॥
4.186.m: Just as the best of elephants rejoice at the roar of rainclouds, / so may your sound bring us joy that carries delight.

4.186.s:
yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso'bhijāyate ..
tathā ca tava śabdena trasyaṃtvasmaddviṣo raṇe..71..( iti duṃdubhimaṃtraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासोऽभिजायते ॥
तथा च तव शब्देन त्रस्यंत्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे॥71॥( इति दुंदुभिमंत्रः ॥)
4.186.m: Just as terror arises in women at the sound of rainclouds, / even so may our enemies tremble in battle at your sound. (Thus the mantra for the war drum.)

4.186.s:
sarvāyudha mahāmātra sarvadevārisūdana ..
cāpa māṃ sarvadā rakṣa sākaṃ sāyakasattamaiḥ .. 72.. ( iti cāpamantraḥ..)
4.186.d:
सर्वायुध महामात्र सर्वदेवारिसूदन ॥
चाप मां सर्वदा रक्ष साकं सायकसत्तमैः ॥ 72॥ ( इति चापमन्त्रः॥)
4.186.m: O commander of all weapons, slayer of all enemies of the gods, / O bow, protect me at all times along with the best of arrows. (Thus the mantra for the bow.)

4.186.s:
puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṣpāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam ..
viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityaṃ manaḥśāṃtiprado bhava .. 73 .. ( iti śaṅkhamantraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
पुण्यस्त्वं शङ्ख पुष्पाणां मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ॥
विष्णुना विधृतो नित्यं मनःशांतिप्रदो भव ॥ 73 ॥ ( इति शङ्खमन्त्रः ॥)
4.186.m: You are holy, O conch, among flowers, and the most auspicious of auspicious things; / constantly held by Viṣṇu, be the bestower of peace of mind. (Thus the mantra for the conch.)

4.186.s:
śaśāṃkakarasaṃkāśa hima ḍiṃḍīrapāṃḍura ..
protsārayāśu duritaṃ cāmarāmaravallabha .. 74 .. ( iti cāmaramaṃtraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
शशांककरसंकाश हिम डिंडीरपांडुर ॥
प्रोत्सारयाशु दुरितं चामरामरवल्लभ ॥ 74 ॥ ( इति चामरमंत्रः ॥)
4.186.m: Resembling moonbeams, white as snow and foam, / quickly drive away misfortune, O chowrie, beloved of the immortals. (Thus the mantra for the chowrie.)

4.186.s:
sarvāyudhānāṃ prathamā nirmitā'si pinākinā ..
śūlāyudhādviniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭiparigraham .. 75 ..
4.186.d:
सर्वायुधानां प्रथमा निर्मिताऽसि पिनाकिना ॥
शूलायुधाद्विनिष्कृष्य कृत्वा मुष्टिपरिग्रहम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.186.m: You were created as the foremost of all weapons by Pinākin, / drawing [you] out from the spear weapon and forming a hilt for the fist.

4.186.s:
caṃḍikāyāḥ pradattāsi sarvaduṣṭanibarhiṇi ..
tathā vistāritā cāsi devānāṃ pratipāditā .. 76 ..
4.186.d:
चंडिकायाः प्रदत्तासि सर्वदुष्टनिबर्हिणि ॥
तथा विस्तारिता चासि देवानां प्रतिपादिता ॥ 76 ॥
4.186.m: You were given to Caṇḍikā, O slayer of all the wicked; / likewise you were multiplied and presented to the gods.

4.186.s:
sarva sattvāṃgabhūtāsi sarvāśubhanivāriṇi ..
churike rakṣa māṃ nityaṃ śāntiṃ yaccha namo'stu te .. 77 .. ( iticchūrikāmaṃtraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
सर्व सत्त्वांगभूतासि सर्वाशुभनिवारिणि ॥
छुरिके रक्ष मां नित्यं शान्तिं यच्छ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 77 ॥ ( इतिच्छूरिकामंत्रः ॥)
4.186.m: You have become a part of the bodies of all beings, / O dispeller of all inauspiciousness! / O dagger, protect me perpetually and grant peace! Homage to you! 77. (Thus the dagger mantra.)

4.186.s:
protsāraṇāya duṣṭānāṃ sādhusaṃgrahaṇāya ca ..
brahmaṇā nirmitaścāsi vyavahāraprasiddhaye ..78..
4.186.d:
प्रोत्सारणाय दुष्टानां साधुसंग्रहणाय च ॥
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितश्चासि व्यवहारप्रसिद्धये ॥78॥
4.186.m: For driving away the wicked and gathering the virtuous, / you were created by Brahmā for the accomplishment of lawful governance.

4.186.s:
yaśo dehi sukhaṃ dehi jagado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
tāḍayāśu ripūnsarvānhemadaṃḍa namostu te .. 79 .. ( iti kanakadaṇḍamantraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
यशो देहि सुखं देहि जगदो भव भूपतेः ॥
ताडयाशु रिपून्सर्वान्हेमदंड नमोस्तु ते ॥ 79 ॥ ( इति कनकदण्डमन्त्रः ॥)
4.186.m: Grant fame, grant happiness, be the protector of the king; / strike down all foes quickly, O golden sceptre, homage to you. (Thus the mantra for the golden sceptre.)

4.186.s:
vijayo jayado jetā ripughātī priyaṃkaraḥ ..
duḥkhahā dharmadaḥ śāṃtaḥ sarvāriṣṭavināśanaḥ ..80..
4.186.d:
विजयो जयदो जेता रिपुघाती प्रियंकरः ॥
दुःखहा धर्मदः शांतः सर्वारिष्टविनाशनः ॥80॥
4.186.m: Vijaya, Jayada, Jetṛ, Ripughātin, Priyaṃkara, / Duḥkhahan, Dharmada, Śānta, and the destroyer of all calamities—

4.186.s:
ete'ṣṭausaṃnidhau yasmāttava siṃhā mahābalāḥ...
tena siṃhāsaneti tvaṃ viprairvedeṣu gīyase ..81..
4.186.d:
एतेऽष्टौसंनिधौ यस्मात्तव सिंहा महाबलाः॥।
तेन सिंहासनेति त्वं विप्रैर्वेदेषु गीयसे ॥81॥
4.186.m: Because these eight mighty lions reside in your presence, / therefore you are praised as 'throne' by the brahmins in the Vedas.

4.186.s:
tvayi sthitaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttvayi śakraḥ sureśvaraḥ..
tvayi sthito harirdevastvadarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ .. 82 ..
4.186.d:
त्वयि स्थितः शिवः साक्षात्त्वयि शक्रः सुरेश्वरः॥
त्वयि स्थितो हरिर्देवस्त्वदर्थं तप्यते तपः ॥ 82 ॥
4.186.m: In you dwells Śiva visibly; in you dwells Śakra, lord of the gods; / in you dwells Lord Hari; for your sake asceticism is performed.

4.186.s:
namaste sarvato bhadra bhadrado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
trailokyajayasarvasva siṃhāsana namo'stu te .. 83 .. ( iti siṃhāsanamaṃtraḥ ..)
4.186.d:
नमस्ते सर्वतो भद्र भद्रदो भव भूपतेः ॥
त्रैलोक्यजयसर्वस्व सिंहासन नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 83 ॥ ( इति सिंहासनमंत्रः ॥)
4.186.m: Homage to you who are auspicious from every side; be the bestower of good fortune upon the king; / O all-in-all of victory in the three worlds, O throne, homage to you. (Thus the mantra for the throne.)

4.186.s:
lohābhihārikaṃ karma kṛtvedaṃ maṃtrapūrvakam..
phalanaivedyakusumairdhūpadīpavilepanaiḥ ..84..
4.186.d:
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कृत्वेदं मंत्रपूर्वकम्॥
फलनैवेद्यकुसुमैर्धूपदीपविलेपनैः ॥84॥
4.186.m: Having performed this iron-lustration rite accompanied by mantras, / with fruits, food-offerings, flowers, incense, lamps, and ointments,

4.186.s: aṣṭamyāṃ dhāvanaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāhṇe snānamācaret.... 85 ..
4.186.d: अष्टम्यां धावनं कृत्वा पूर्वाह्णे स्नानमाचरेत्॥॥ 85 ॥
4.186.m: and having cleansed [oneself] on the aṣṭamī, one should take a bath in the morning.

4.186.s:
( atha gadyam)
durgāṃ kāṃcanamūrtiṃ raupyāṃ vā paittalīṃ vārkṣī caitrīṃ tāmrīṃ vādhibhavataḥ kṛtvā dāruvicitratoraṇavinyastāṃ śobhane sthāne purato vinyastadṛṣṭāṃ vicitragṛhamadhyagāṃ snātāṃ kuṃkumacaṃdanagaṃdhaiścatuḥsamaiścīrapaṭṭaiścarcitagātrāṃ devīṃ kusumairabhyarcya tāṃ bahubhiḥ puṣyamāṇakīrtistairdvijananairjanitaparitoṣairdivānvito nareṃdraḥ svayaṃ prayacchetpurohitaiḥ sārdhaṃ bilvapatreṇārcanena maṃtreṇānena bhagavatyai ..
( iti gadyaṃ sampūrṇaṃ) ..
jayaṃtī maṃgalā kālī bhadrakālī kapālinī ..
durgā śivā kṣamā dhātrī svāhā svadhā namostu te .. 86 ..
4.186.d:
( अथ गद्यम्)
दुर्गां कांचनमूर्तिं रौप्यां वा पैत्तलीं वार्क्षी चैत्रीं ताम्रीं वाधिभवतः कृत्वा दारुविचित्रतोरणविन्यस्तां शोभने स्थाने पुरतो विन्यस्तदृष्टां विचित्रगृहमध्यगां स्नातां कुंकुमचंदनगंधैश्चतुःसमैश्चीरपट्टैश्चर्चितगात्रां देवीं कुसुमैरभ्यर्च्य तां बहुभिः पुष्यमाणकीर्तिस्तैर्द्विजननैर्जनितपरितोषैर्दिवान्वितो नरेंद्रः स्वयं प्रयच्छेत्पुरोहितैः सार्धं बिल्वपत्रेणार्चनेन मंत्रेणानेन भगवत्यै ॥
( इति गद्यं सम्पूर्णं) ॥
जयंती मंगला काली भद्रकाली कपालिनी ॥
दुर्गा शिवा क्षमा धात्री स्वाहा स्वधा नमोस्तु ते ॥ 86 ॥
4.186.m:
(Now the prose passage:)
Having made an image of Durgā—golden, silver, brass, wooden, painted, or copper—according to his means, placed beneath a wondrous wooden arch in a beautiful spot, with her gaze directed forward, stationed in the middle of a splendid house, bathed, her limbs smeared with saffron, sandalwood paste, fragrant mixtures of four scents, and fine silken cloth, the king, accompanied by many twice-born men whose fame is flourishing and who are brought satisfaction, should himself, along with the royal priests, present worship to the Goddess with bilva leaves and flowers by day with this mantra: (End of the prose passage)
Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī, / Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā, Svadhā, homage to you.

4.186.s:
amṛtodbhavaḥ śrīvṛkṣo mahādevīpriyaḥ sadā ..
bilvapatraṃ prayacchāmi pavitraṃ te sureśvari .. 87 ..
4.186.d:
अमृतोद्भवः श्रीवृक्षो महादेवीप्रियः सदा ॥
बिल्वपत्रं प्रयच्छामि पवित्रं ते सुरेश्वरि ॥ 87 ॥
4.186.m: Born from nectar, the holy tree is ever dear to the Great Goddess; / I offer you a pure bilva leaf, O ruler of the gods.

4.186.s:
durgā saṃpūjanīyā ca taddināddroṇapuṣpayā ..
sā cābhīṣṭā sureśānyāstathā rūḍhavraṇāyutaḥ ...88...
4.186.d:
दुर्गा संपूजनीया च तद्दिनाद्द्रोणपुष्पया ॥
सा चाभीष्टा सुरेशान्यास्तथा रूढव्रणायुतः ॥.88॥।
4.186.m: And Durgā should be worshipped from that day with droṇapuṣpa flowers; / for she is cherished by the queen of the gods, and one [who worships her] is freed from old wounds.

4.186.s:
tataḥ khaḍgaṃ namaskṛtya śatrūṇāṃ mānamarddanam ..
icchetsvavijayaṃ rājyaṃ subhikṣaṃ cātmano nṛpa .. 89 ..
4.186.d:
ततः खड्गं नमस्कृत्य शत्रूणां मानमर्द्दनम् ॥
इच्छेत्स्वविजयं राज्यं सुभिक्षं चात्मनो नृप ॥ 89 ॥
4.186.m: Then, having bowed to the sword, the crusher of the pride of enemies, / the king should desire his own victory, kingdom, and abundance of food.

4.186.s:
punaḥ punaḥ praṇamyātha dhyāyecca hṛdaye śivām..
mahiṣaghrīṃ bahubhujāṃ kumārīṃ siṃhavāhinīm .. 90 ..
4.186.d:
पुनः पुनः प्रणम्याथ ध्यायेच्च हृदये शिवाम्॥
महिषघ्रीं बहुभुजां कुमारीं सिंहवाहिनीम् ॥ 90 ॥
4.186.m: Having bowed again and again, he should then meditate in his heart on Śivā, / the slayer of Mahiṣa, many-armed, a maiden, riding a lion,

4.186.s:
dānavāṃstarjayaṃtīṃ ca khaḍgoddhatakarāṃ śubhām ..
ghaṃṭākṣasragdharāṃ durgāṃ raṇāraṃbhe vyavasthitām .. 91 ..
4.186.d:
दानवांस्तर्जयंतीं च खड्गोद्धतकरां शुभाम् ॥
घंटाक्षस्रग्धरां दुर्गां रणारंभे व्यवस्थिताम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.186.m: threatening the Dānavas, her auspicious hand raised with a sword, / holding a bell and a rosary, Durgā standing at the onset of battle.

4.186.s: tato jayajayākāraiḥ stavaṃ kuryādimaṃ tataḥ .. 92 ..
4.186.d: ततो जयजयाकारैः स्तवं कुर्यादिमं ततः ॥ 92 ॥
4.186.m: Then, with shouts of victory, he should then recite this hymn of praise:

4.186.s:
sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike ..
śaraṇye tryaṃbake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te .. 93 ..
4.186.d:
सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके ॥
शरण्ये त्र्यंबके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 93 ॥
4.186.m: O most auspicious of all auspicious things, O Śivā, accomplisher of all aims, / O refuge, O three-eyed one, O Gaurī, O Nārāyaṇī, homage to you.

4.186.s:
kuṃkumena samālabdhe candanena vilepite ..
bilvapatrakṛtāmāle durge'haṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ..94..
4.186.d:
कुंकुमेन समालब्धे चन्दनेन विलेपिते ॥
बिल्वपत्रकृतामाले दुर्गेऽहं शरणं गतः ॥94॥
4.186.m: Smeared with saffron, anointed with sandalwood paste, / garlanded with bilva leaves, O Durgā, I have come to you for refuge.

4.186.s:
kṛtvaivamarccāṃ kauravya aṣṭamyāṃ jāgaraṃ niśi ..
naṭanartanagītaiśca kārayettu mahotsavam ..95..
4.186.d:
कृत्वैवमर्च्चां कौरव्य अष्टम्यां जागरं निशि ॥
नटनर्तनगीतैश्च कारयेत्तु महोत्सवम् ॥95॥
4.186.m: Having performed the worship thus, O descendant of Kuru, on the aṣṭamī he should keep a vigil at night / and cause a great festival to be held with actors, dances, and songs.

4.186.s:
evaṃ hṛṣṭairniśāṃ nītvā prabhāte cāruṇodaye ..
pātayenmahiṣānmeṣānagrato natakandharān ..96..
4.186.d:
एवं हृष्टैर्निशां नीत्वा प्रभाते चारुणोदये ॥
पातयेन्महिषान्मेषानग्रतो नतकन्धरान् ॥96॥
4.186.m: Having thus spent the night joyfully, at daybreak when the dawn rises, / he should strike down buffaloes and rams, their necks bowed forward,

4.186.s:
śataṃ cāpi śatārdhaṃ vā tadarddhaṃ vā yathecchayā ..
surāsavabhṛtaiḥ kuṃbhaistarpayetparameśvarīm .. 97 ..
4.186.d:
शतं चापि शतार्धं वा तदर्द्धं वा यथेच्छया ॥
सुरासवभृतैः कुंभैस्तर्पयेत्परमेश्वरीम् ॥ 97 ॥
4.186.m: one hundred, or fifty, or half of that, according to his wish, / and satisfy Parameśvarī with jars filled with spirituous liquor.

4.186.s:
kāpālikebhyastaddeyaṃ dāsīdāsajanaistathā ..
vibhajya sarvaṃ kauṃteya suhṛtsaṃbaṃdhibaṃdhuṣu ..98..
4.186.d:
कापालिकेभ्यस्तद्देयं दासीदासजनैस्तथा ॥
विभज्य सर्वं कौंतेय सुहृत्संबंधिबंधुषु ॥98॥
4.186.m: That should be given to Kāpālikas, and likewise by female and male servants / distributed completely, O son of Kuntī, among friends, relations, and kinsmen.

4.186.s:
tatoparāhṇasamaye navamyāṃ syaṃdane sthitām ..
bhavānīṃ bhrāmayedrāṣṭre svayaṃ rājā sasainyavān ..99..
4.186.d:
ततोपराह्णसमये नवम्यां स्यंदने स्थिताम् ॥
भवानीं भ्रामयेद्राष्ट्रे स्वयं राजा ससैन्यवान् ॥99॥
4.186.m: Then in the afternoon on the navamī, the king himself, accompanied by his army, / should process Bhavānī through the realm as she stands on a chariot,

4.186.s:
sahasraiḥ puruṣairvāpi rathayuktaiḥ suśikṣitaiḥ ..
śanaiḥ śanairadhikayā dīptyā prajvaladīpakaiḥ ..100..
4.186.d:
सहस्रैः पुरुषैर्वापि रथयुक्तैः सुशिक्षितैः ॥
शनैः शनैरधिकया दीप्त्या प्रज्वलदीपकैः ॥100॥
4.186.m: or with thousands of men harnessed to the chariot and well trained, / slowly, with blazing lamps of intense brilliance,

4.186.s:
ākṛṣṭakhaḍgairvīraiśca dhāturaktairgajaistathā ..
nadadbhiḥ śaṃkhapaṭahairnṛtyadbhirvārayauvataiḥ ..
alaṃkṛtābhirnārībhirbālakaiḥ suvibhūṣitaiḥ ..101..
4.186.d:
आकृष्टखड्गैर्वीरैश्च धातुरक्तैर्गजैस्तथा ॥
नदद्भिः शंखपटहैर्नृत्यद्भिर्वारयौवतैः ॥
अलंकृताभिर्नारीभिर्बालकैः सुविभूषितैः ॥101॥
4.186.m: and with heroes with drawn swords, with elephants painted red with mineral dyes, / with sounding conches and kettledrums, with dancing courtesans, / adorned women, and well-ornamented boys.

4.186.s:
bhūtebhyastu baliṃ dadyānmaṃtreṇānena sāmiṣam ..
saraktaṃ sajalaṃ sānnaṃ gandhapuṣpākṣatairyutam ..1 02..
4.186.d:
भूतेभ्यस्तु बलिं दद्यान्मंत्रेणानेन सामिषम् ॥
सरक्तं सजलं सान्नं गन्धपुष्पाक्षतैर्युतम् ॥1 02॥
4.186.m: He should present an offering containing meat to the ghosts with this mantra, / accompanied by blood, water, food, and fragrant flowers and unhusked barley grains.

4.186.s:
trīṃstrīnvārāṃstriśūlena digvidikṣu kṣipedbalim ..
baliṃ gṛhṇantvimaṃ devā ādityā vasavastathā .. 103 ..
4.186.d:
त्रींस्त्रीन्वारांस्त्रिशूलेन दिग्विदिक्षु क्षिपेद्बलिम् ॥
बलिं गृह्णन्त्विमं देवा आदित्या वसवस्तथा ॥ 103 ॥
4.186.m: Three times each with a trident he should cast the offering into the cardinal and intermediate directions: / 'May the gods take this offering, as well as the Ādityas and the Vasus,

4.186.s:
maruto'thāśvinau rudrāḥ suparṇāḥ pannagā grahāḥ ..
asurā yātudhānāśca mātaraśca piśācakāḥ .. 104
4.186.d:
मरुतोऽथाश्विनौ रुद्राः सुपर्णाः पन्नगा ग्रहाः ॥
असुरा यातुधानाश्च मातरश्च पिशाचकाः ॥ 104
4.186.m: the Maruts, the two Aśvins, the Rudras, the birds, the serpents, the planets, / the asuras, the yātudhānas, the mothers, and the piśācas,

4.186.s:
śākinyo yakṣavetālā yoginyaḥ pūtanāḥ śivāḥ ..
jṛṃbhakāḥ siddhagandharvā vyālā vidyādharā dharāḥ.. 105..
4.186.d:
शाकिन्यो यक्षवेताला योगिन्यः पूतनाः शिवाः ॥
जृंभकाः सिद्धगन्धर्वा व्याला विद्याधरा धराः॥ 105॥
4.186.m: the śākinīs, yakṣas, vetālas, yoginīs, pūtanās, jackals, / jṛmbhakas, siddhas, gandharvas, beasts of prey, vidyādharas, and spirits of the earth,

4.186.s:
dikpālā lokapālāśca ye ca vighnavināyakāḥ ..
jagatāṃ śāṃtikartāro brahmādyāśca maharṣayaḥ ..106..
4.186.d:
दिक्पाला लोकपालाश्च ये च विघ्नविनायकाः ॥
जगतां शांतिकर्तारो ब्रह्माद्याश्च महर्षयः ॥106॥
4.186.m: the guardians of the directions, the world protectors, and those who are vināyakas causing obstacles, / the makers of peace for the worlds, and the great sages headed by Brahmā.

4.186.s:
savighnaṃ mama pāpaṃ te śāmyaṃtu paripanthinaḥ..
saumyā bhavaṃtu tṛptāśca bhūtāḥ pretāḥ sukhāvahāḥ ..107..
ityevaṃ bhrāmayedrāṣṭre durgāṃ devīṃ rathe sthitām..
narayānena vā pārtha tato'vighnaṃ samāpayet ..1 08..
athotpanneṣu vighneṣu bhūtaśāṃtiṃ samācaret ..
yena vighnā na jāyaṃte yātrāsaṃpūrṇatāṃ vrajet..1 09..
evaṃ ye kurvate yātrāṃ rājāno'nye'pi mānavāḥ..
mahānavamyāṃ naṃdāyāṃ putrakā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ ..11 0..
te sarve pāpanirmuktā yāṃti bhāgavatīṃ purīm ..1 11..
4.186.d:
सविघ्नं मम पापं ते शाम्यंतु परिपन्थिनः॥
सौम्या भवंतु तृप्ताश्च भूताः प्रेताः सुखावहाः ॥107॥
इत्येवं भ्रामयेद्राष्ट्रे दुर्गां देवीं रथे स्थिताम्॥
नरयानेन वा पार्थ ततोऽविघ्नं समापयेत् ॥1 08॥
अथोत्पन्नेषु विघ्नेषु भूतशांतिं समाचरेत् ॥
येन विघ्ना न जायंते यात्रासंपूर्णतां व्रजेत्॥1 09॥
एवं ये कुर्वते यात्रां राजानोऽन्येऽपि मानवाः॥
महानवम्यां नंदायां पुत्रका हृष्टमानसाः ॥11 0॥
ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यांति भागवतीं पुरीम् ॥1 11॥
4.186.m:
May my sins along with obstacles be pacified; may my adversaries be quieted; / may the ghosts and pretas be gentle, satisfied, and bringers of happiness.'
In this manner he should process Goddess Durgā through the realm, standing on a chariot / or in a palanquin, O son of Pṛthā, and then bring it to a close without obstacles.
Now, if obstacles arise, one should perform the pacification of ghosts, / whereby obstacles do not arise, and the procession attains completion.
Thus, the kings and other men who perform the procession / on Mahānavamī, the joyful day, with cheerful minds, [having obtained] sons,
all of them, freed from sin, go to the city of the Lord.

4.186.s:
na teṣāṃ śāvakonāgnirna caurā na vināyakāḥ ..
vighnaṃ kurvanti rājendra yeṣāṃ tuṣṭā maheśvarī .. 112 ..
4.186.d:
न तेषां शावकोनाग्निर्न चौरा न विनायकाः ॥
विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति राजेन्द्र येषां तुष्टा महेश्वरी ॥ 112 ॥
4.186.m: Neither lightning nor fire, nor thieves nor vināyakas, / create obstacles for them, O king of kings, with whom Maheśvarī is pleased.

4.186.s:
nīrujaḥ sukhino bhogabhoktāro bhayavarjitāḥ..
bhavaṃti bhaktāḥ puruṣāḥ bhagavatyāḥ kimucyate .. 113 ..
4.186.d:
नीरुजः सुखिनो भोगभोक्तारो भयवर्जिताः॥
भवंति भक्ताः पुरुषाः भगवत्याः किमुच्यते ॥ 113 ॥
4.186.m: Men who are devotees of the Goddess become free from disease, / happy, enjoyers of pleasures, and free from fear; what more can be said?

4.186.s:
ityeṣa te samākhyāto durgādevyā mahotsavaḥ ..
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvāśubhavināśanaḥ .. 114 ..
4.186.d:
इत्येष ते समाख्यातो दुर्गादेव्या महोत्सवः ॥
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव सर्वाशुभविनाशनः ॥ 114 ॥
4.186.m: Thus has this great festival of the goddess Durgā been related to you; / for those who recite it and hear it, it destroys all inauspiciousness.

4.186.s:
śūlāgrabhinnamahiṣāsurapṛṣṭhaviṣṭāmṛtakhātakhaḍgarucirāṃgadabāhudaṇḍām ..
abhyarcya paṃcavadanānugatāṃ navamyāṃ durgāṃ sudurgagahanāni taraṃti martyāḥ .. 115 ..
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
puṇyā mahānavamyasti tithīnāṃ pravarā tithiḥ..
sānuṣṭheyā suraiḥ sarvaiḥ prajāpālairviśeṣataḥ..1..

भूतप्रेतपिशाचानां प्रीत्यर्थं चोत्सवाय वा ॥ 2 ॥
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
कस्मात्कालात्प्रवृत्तेयं नवमी महशब्दयुक् ॥
किमादावुपान्नोऽस्ति भगवन्नवमीविधिः ॥ 3 ॥
यशोदागर्भसंभूतेरुत यात्रा प्रवर्तते ॥

यदस्यां प्राणिनः केचिन्मन्यंते घातयंति च ॥
हतानां प्राणिनां तेषां का गतिः पारलौकिकी ॥ 5 ॥
स्वयं घ्नतां घातयतामनुमोदयतां तथा ॥
एतन्मे संशयं पूर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि केशव ॥ 6 ॥
4.186.m:
Having worshipped on the navamī Durgā, who stands upon the back of Mahiṣāsura pierced by the tip of her trident, / whose arm-staffs bear armlets gleaming with unsheathed swords, and who is attended by the five-faced [Śiva], mortals cross over impassable difficulties.
The Blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / The holy Mahānavamī is the foremost lunar day among lunar days; / it should be observed by all gods, and especially by rulers of people.
O son of Pṛthā, you should celebrate it indeed for happiness throughout the year, / or for the delight of ghosts, pretas, and piśācas, and as a festival.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: / From what time did this navamī, joined with the word "mahā", begin? / O Blessed One, was the rite of the navamī established at the very beginning?
Does this procession proceed from her birth in the womb of Yaśodā, / or was it already present formerly, in the Kṛta, Tretā, and other yugas?
Since on this [day] some people intend [offerings] and slay living beings, / what is the fate in the next world for those slain beings,
and for those who themselves kill, who cause [others] to kill, and who approve [of it]? / You ought first to explain this doubt of mine, O Keśava.

॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पार्थ या परमा शक्तिरनंता लोकविश्रुता ॥
आद्या सर्वगता शुद्धा भाव गम्या मनोहरा ॥ 7 ॥
आद्याष्टमी कलाकाली द्वितीया सर्वमंगला ॥
माया कात्यायनी दुर्गा चामुंडा शंकरप्रिया ॥ 8 ॥
ध्यायंति यां योगरतां सा देवी परमेश्वरी ॥
रूपभेदैर्नामभेदैर्भवानी पूज्यते शिवा॥9॥
अष्टम्यां तु नवम्यां तु देवदानवराक्षसैः॥
गंधर्वैरुरगैर्यज्ञैः पूज्यते किन्नरैर्नरैः॥10॥
अन्येष्वपि युगेष्वादौ सृष्टेः पूर्वं प्रदर्शिता॥
पूज्यतेयं पुरा देवी तेभ्यः पूर्वतरैः शुभैः॥11॥
आश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षे च याष्टमी मूल संयुता ॥
सा महानवमी नाम त्रैलोक्येऽपि सुदुर्लभा ॥ 12 ॥
कन्यागते सवितरि शुक्लपक्षेऽष्टमी तु या ॥
मूलनक्षत्रसंयुक्ता सा महानवमी स्मृता ॥ 13 ॥
4.186.m:
The Blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / O son of Pṛthā, she who is the supreme Power, infinite, world-renowned, / the primordial, all-pervading, pure, accessible through devotion, and captivating;
the primordial eighth, the digit Kālī, the second, Sarvamaṅgalā, / Māyā, Kātyāyanī, Durgā, Cāmuṇḍā, beloved of Śaṅkara;
that Goddess, Parameśvarī, upon whom those devoted to yoga meditate— / as Bhavānī, Śivā, she is worshipped through various forms and various names.
On the aṣṭamī and on the navamī, by gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas, / by gandharvas, serpents, yajñas, kinnaras, and men she is worshipped.
Even in other yugas, shown at the beginning before creation, / this Goddess was worshipped in ancient times by auspicious beings even earlier than they.
And in the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, the aṣṭamī that is conjoined with Mūla / is called Mahānavamī, very difficult to attain even in the three worlds.
When the sun has entered Virgo, the aṣṭamī in the bright fortnight / that is conjoined with the asterism Mūla is traditionally regarded as Mahānavamī.

4.186.d:
अष्टम्यां च नवम्यां च जगन्मातरमम्बिकाम् ॥
पूजयित्वा'ऽश्विने मासि विशोको जयति द्विषः ॥ 14 ॥
संतर्जयंती हुंकारैः खड्गादिभिरहर्निशम् ॥
नवम्यां पूजिता देवी ददाति नवमं फलम् ॥ 15 ॥
सा पुण्या सा पवित्रा च सा धर्मसुखदायिनी ॥
तस्मात्सदा पूजनीया चामुंडा मुंडमालिनी ॥ 16 ॥
तस्यां यद्युपयुज्यंते प्राणिनो महिषादयः ॥
सर्वे ते स्वर्गतिं यांति घ्नतां पापं न विद्यते ॥ 17 ॥
न तथा बलिदानेन पुष्पधूपविलेपनैः ॥
यथा संतुष्यते लोके महिषैर्विंध्यवासिनी ॥ 18 ॥
उद्दिश्य दुर्गां हन्यंते विधानाद्येऽत्र जंतवः ॥
स्वर्गं ते यांति कौंतेय घातयंतोऽपि भक्तिः ॥ 19 ॥
भवानीप्राङ्गणे प्राणा येषां याता युधिष्ठिर ॥
तेषां स्वर्गे ध्रुवं वासो वरास्तेऽप्यरसां प्रियाः ॥ 20 ॥
4.186.m:
Having worshipped the Mother of the World, Ambikā, on the aṣṭamī and navamī / in the month of Āśvina, one conquers enemies, free from sorrow.
Menacing day and night with hum-cries and swords and other [weapons], / the Goddess, worshipped on the navamī, grants a fresh reward.
She is meritorious, she is pure, she is the giver of virtue and happiness; / therefore, Cāmuṇḍā, adorned with a garland of heads, should always be worshipped.
If on that [day] creatures such as buffaloes are sacrificed, / they all attain heaven, and no sin accrues to those who kill them.
Vindhyavāsinī is not so pleased in the world by animal sacrifice, / nor by flowers, incense, and ointments, as she is by buffaloes.
The creatures that are slain here according to the prescribed rule, dedicated to Durgā, / go to heaven, O son of Kuntī, and those who cause them to be slain with devotion [reap merit].
Those whose lives depart in the courtyard of Bhavānī, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / have a permanent dwelling in heaven; they become best among men, dear to the apsarases.

4.186.m:
In all the manvantaras and kalpas, O delight of the Kurus, / in all of them, this navamī was worshipped in ancient times.
Celebrated, without beginning or end, year after year, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / through repeated incarnations Bhavānī is worshipped by the gods.
Always descended to the earth, the perpetual slayer of daityas, / she maintains order in heaven, the netherworld, and the mortal realm.
And again, this Great Goddess, born from the womb of Yaśodā, / placed her foot on the head of the demon Kaṃsa, whose life had run out.
From that time forward, having established on Mount Vindhya / her who brought joy to Yaśodā, her worship was initiated anew in the worlds.
Though already flourishing earlier, the majesty of my sister was manifested once more / on earth for the welfare of all and for the pacification of all afflictions.
Thus, fasting for the Navarātra of Vindhyavāsinī, / or with a one-night fast, or a nocturnal meal, according to one's capability, or with unsolicited food,
the gods [are worshipped] with sacrifices and priestly services in every place, in every city, / in every house, by those intent on devotion, in every village, in every forest,

by bathed, cheerful, and glad brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, kings, / vaiśyas, and śūdras, with varied devotions, by mlecchas and other men,
and by women, O bull of the Kurus; hear now this procedure for it: / A king desirous of victory, starting from the first day [of the fortnight] in regular succession,
should cause the iron-lustration rite to be performed up to the aṣṭamī. / In a place sloping to the north-east, decorated with flags,
he should cause an excellent celestial pavilion to be built, measuring nine by seven cubits; / in the south-east he should cause a sacrificial pit to be made, measuring a cubit, very beautiful,
endowed with three girdles, having a yoni shaped like an aśvattha leaf. / All the insignia of royalty, and whatever weapons and missiles there are,
having brought them to the pavilion, he should consecrate them all. / Then a brāhmaṇa, bathed, wearing white garments, pure,
should offer clarified butter with mantras preceded by the syllable Oṃ and bearing their characteristic marks. (35cd)
Formerly there was an exceedingly powerful dānava named Loha. (36ab)

तदंगसम्भवं लोहं यत्सर्वंदृश्यते क्षितौ ॥ 36 ॥
शस्त्रास्त्रमन्त्रैर्होतव्यं पायसं घृतसंयुतम् ॥
हुतशेषं तुरंगाणां गजानामुपहारयेत् ॥ 37 ॥
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म तेनैतदृषिभिः स्मृतम् ॥
बद्धप्रतिशरव्यं च गजाश्वसमलंकृतम् ॥ 38 ॥
भ्रामयेन्नगरे नित्यं नंदि घोषपुरस्सरम्॥
प्रत्यहं नृपतिः स्नात्वा संपूज्य पितृदेवताः ॥ 39 ॥
पूजयेद्राजचिह्नानि फलमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥
हुतशेषं प्रदातव्यमौपनायनिके द्विजे ॥ 40 ॥
तस्याभिहरणाद्राज्ञो विजयः समुदाहृतः ॥
पूजामंत्रान्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणोक्तानहं तव ॥ 41 ॥
यैः पूजिताः प्रयच्छन्ति कीर्तिमायु र्यशोबलम॥
यथांबुदश्छादयति शिवायेमां वसुन्धराम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.186.m:
he was hacked to pieces in various ways by the enraged gods in battle; / all the iron that is seen on earth originated from his body.
An oblation of milk-rice mixed with ghee should be offered with the mantras for weapons and missiles; / the remainder of the oblation should be presented to the horses and elephants.
Therefore, this is remembered by the sages as the iron-lustration rite; / targets are set up, and it is adorned with elephants and horses.
he should parade [them] daily around the city, preceded by joyful cries.
Every day, having bathed and worshipped the ancestors and deities,
the king should worship the insignia of royalty with fruits, garlands, and ointments.
The remainder of the offering should be given to an initiated twice-born [brahmin].
Victory is proclaimed for the king from its presentation.
I will tell you the worship mantras taught in the Purāṇas,
worshipped with which, they bestow fame, long life, renown, and strength.
Just as a cloud covers this earth for its welfare,

4.186.s:
tathācchādaya rājānaṃ vijayārogyavṛddhaye .. ( iti chatramantraḥ) ..
gandharva kulajātastvaṃ mābhūyāḥ kuladūṣakaḥ .. 43 ..
brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca ..
prabhāvāñca hutāśasya varddhasva tvaṃ turaṃgama .. 44 ..

rudrasya brahmacaryeṇa pavanasya valena ca.. smṛ ..

sūryācandramasau vāyuḥ pāvakaśca na yatra vai .. 47..

vikṛtiṃ yadi gacchestvaṃ yuddhedhvani turaṃgama ..

4.186.d:
तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये ॥ ( इति छत्रमन्त्रः) ॥
गन्धर्व कुलजातस्त्वं माभूयाः कुलदूषकः ॥ 43 ॥
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥
प्रभावाञ्च हुताशस्य वर्द्धस्व त्वं तुरंगम ॥ 44 ॥
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसा यथा ॥
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य वलेन च॥ स्मृ ॥
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रोऽसि कौस्तुभं च मणिं स्मर ॥
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत्पितृहा मातृहा तथा ॥ 46 ॥
भूम्यर्थेनृतवादी च क्षत्रियश्च पराङ्मुखः ॥
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुः पावकश्च न यत्र वै ॥ 47॥
व्रजेच्च तां गतिं क्षिप्रं तच्च पापं भवेत्किल ॥
विकृतिं यदि गच्छेस्त्वं युद्धेध्वनि तुरंगम ॥
रिपून्विजित्य समरे सह भर्त्रा सुखी भव ॥ 48 ॥॥ ॥ ( इत्यश्वमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.186.m:
so cover the king, for the increase of victory and health. (Thus the royal parasol mantra.)
You are born from the Gandharva race; do not be a defiler of your race.
By the true word of Brahmā, of Soma, and of Varuṇa,
and by the power of the Fire-god, increase, O horse!
By the splendour of the Sun, as by the ascetic heat of the sages,
by the celibacy of Rudra, and by the strength of the Wind,
remember: you are a prince! And remember the Kaustubha jewel!
The destination that a killer of a brahmin would reach, or a killer of a father, or a killer of a mother,
and one who speaks falsehood for the sake of land, and a kṣatriya who turns his back [in battle],
where indeed the sun and moon, the wind, and the fire do not reach,
to that destination he would quickly go, and that sin would surely be [yours],
if you should become recalcitrant in battle on the march, O horse!
Conquering the enemies in battle, be happy together with your master! (Thus the horse mantra.)

4.186.s:
śakraketo mahāvīrya suparṇastvayyupasthitaḥ ..
patatrirāḍvainateyastathā nārāyaṇadhvajaḥ .. 49 ..
kāśyapeyo'mṛto jñeyo nāgārirviṣṇuvāhanaḥ ..
aprameyo durādharṣo devaśatruniṣūdanaḥ .. 50 ..
garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ ..
śastravarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣāsmāṃśca ripūndaha .. 51 .. .. (iti dhvajamaṃtraḥ) .. ..
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadaṃto'tha vāmanaḥ ..
supratīkoñjano nīla ete'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ .... 52 ..
eteṣāṃ putrapautrāśca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ ..
bhadro mandro mṛgaścaiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca ..
vanevane prasūtāste kariyoniṃ mahāgajāḥ..53..
pātu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ ..
bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaṃ pratipālayan .. 54 ..
4.186.d:
शक्रकेतो महावीर्य सुपर्णस्त्वय्युपस्थितः ॥
पतत्रिराड्वैनतेयस्तथा नारायणध्वजः ॥ 49 ॥
काश्यपेयोऽमृतो ज्ञेयो नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः ॥
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो देवशत्रुनिषूदनः ॥ 50 ॥
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः ॥
शस्त्रवर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्मांश्च रिपून्दह ॥ 51 ॥ ॥ (इति ध्वजमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदंतोऽथ वामनः ॥
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नील एतेऽष्टौ देवयोनयः ॥॥ 52 ॥
एतेषां पुत्रपौत्राश्च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः ॥
भद्रो मन्द्रो मृगश्चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च ॥
वनेवने प्रसूतास्ते करियोनिं महागजाः॥53॥
पातु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः ॥
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयं प्रतिपालयन् ॥ 54 ॥
4.186.m:
O flag of Indra, of mighty valor, the fair-winged [Garuḍa] is present in you,
the king of birds, the son of Vinatā, and the banner of Nārāyaṇa.
He should be known as the son of Kaśyapa, immortal, enemy of the serpents, the mount of Viṣṇu,
immeasurable, invincible, slayer of the enemies of the gods.
Winged Garuḍa, moving with the swiftness of the wind, is placed and abides in you.
Protect the weapons, armour, and warriors, and protect us, and burn the enemies! (Thus the banner mantra.)
Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana,
Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla: these are the eight of divine origin.
Their sons and grandsons, resorted to by the eight armies—
Bhadra, Mandra, and Mṛga, and the Mixed elephant—
those great elephants born in forest after forest, of the elephant species:
may the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas, along with the Marut hosts, protect you.
Protect your master, O lord of elephants, keeping your compact.

4.186.s:
avāpurhi jayaṃ yuddhe gamane svasti no vraja ..
śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavonilāt ..
sthairyaṃ merorjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devātpuraṃdarāt .. 55 ..
yuddhe rakṣaṃtu nāgāstvāṃ diśaśca saha daivataiḥ ..
aśvinau saha gaṃdharvaiḥ pāṃtu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā .. 56 .. ( iti hastimaṃtraḥ ..)
hutabhugvasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ ..
nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣa bhūtagaṇāgrahāḥ .. 57 ..
pramathāśca sahādityairbhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha ..
śakrasenāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritāstvayi .. 58 ..
pradahaṃtu ripūnsarvānrājā vijayamṛcchatu ..
yāni prayuktānyaribhirdūṣaṇāni samaṃtataḥ .. 59 ..
etāni paraśatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā ..
kālanemivadhe yuddhe yuddhe tripuraghātane .. 60 ..
hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe yuddhe devāsure tathā ..
śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhamānāstu bhūpateḥ .. 61 ..
4.186.d:
अवापुर्हि जयं युद्धे गमने स्वस्ति नो व्रज ॥
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवोनिलात् ॥
स्थैर्यं मेरोर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात्पुरंदरात् ॥ 55 ॥
युद्धे रक्षंतु नागास्त्वां दिशश्च सह दैवतैः ॥
अश्विनौ सह गंधर्वैः पांतु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥ 56 ॥ ( इति हस्तिमंत्रः ॥)
हुतभुग्वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः ॥
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्ष भूतगणाग्रहाः ॥ 57 ॥
प्रमथाश्च सहादित्यैर्भूतेशो मातृभिः सह ॥
शक्रसेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितास्त्वयि ॥ 58 ॥
प्रदहंतु रिपून्सर्वान्राजा विजयमृच्छतु ॥
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्दूषणानि समंततः ॥ 59 ॥
एतानि परशत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा ॥
कालनेमिवधे युद्धे युद्धे त्रिपुरघातने ॥ 60 ॥
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे युद्धे देवासुरे तथा ॥
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभमानास्तु भूपतेः ॥ 61 ॥
4.186.m:
For they attained victory in battle; advance for our welfare on the march!
May your beauty be from Soma, strength from Viṣṇu, splendour from the Sun, speed from the Wind,
stability from Meru, victory from Rudra, and fame from the divine Indra.
May the serpents protect you in battle, and the directions together with their deities;
may the two Aśvins together with the Gandharvas protect you on all sides always. (Thus the elephant mantra.)
The Fire-god, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Wind, Soma, the great sages,
serpents, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakṣas, hosts of ghosts, and the planets,
and the Pramathas along with the Ādityas, the Lord of Ghosts with the Mothers,
Indra’s army commander Skanda, and Varuṇa are lodged in you.
May they burn all enemies; may the king attain victory!
Whatever corruptions have been employed all around by enemies,
these of the enemy’s forces are destroyed by your splendour!
In the battle of the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle of the destruction of Tripura,
in the battle against Hiraṇyakaśipu, and likewise in the battle between the gods and the asuras,
you shone; in that very way, shine today for the king!

4.186.s:
nīlāṃ śvetāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā naśyaṃtvadya nṛpārayaḥ ..
vyādhibhirvividhairghoraiḥ śastraiśca yudhi nirjitāḥ .. 62 ..
sadyaḥ svasthā bhavaṃti sma tvadvātenāpamārjitāḥ .. 63 ..
pūtanā revatī nāmnā kālarātrīti yā smṛtā ..
dahaṃtvāśu ripūnsarvānpatāke tvāmupāgatāḥ .. 64 .. (iti patākāmantraḥ ..)
asiśca ripuhā khaḍgastīkṣṇakarmā durāsadaḥ ..
śrīgarbho vijayaścaiva dharmadhārastathaiva ca .. 69 ..
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni svayamuktāni vedhasā ..
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ .. 66 ..
hiraṇyaṃ ca śarīraṃte dhātā devojanārdanaḥ ..
pitā pitāmaho devastvaṃ māṃ pālaya sarvadā .. 67 .. (iti khaḍgamantraḥ ..)
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varma sarvāyaso hyasi ..
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo'haṃ tava varmannamo'stu te .. 68 .. ( iti varmamantraḥ ..) ..
4.186.d:
नीलां श्वेतामिमां दृष्ट्वा नश्यंत्वद्य नृपारयः ॥
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर्घोरैः शस्त्रैश्च युधि निर्जिताः ॥ 62 ॥
सद्यः स्वस्था भवंति स्म त्वद्वातेनापमार्जिताः ॥ 63 ॥
पूतना रेवती नाम्ना कालरात्रीति या स्मृता ॥
दहंत्वाशु रिपून्सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपागताः ॥ 64 ॥ (इति पताकामन्त्रः ॥)
असिश्च रिपुहा खड्गस्तीक्ष्णकर्मा दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मधारस्तथैव च ॥ 69 ॥
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि स्वयमुक्तानि वेधसा ॥
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः ॥ 66 ॥
हिरण्यं च शरीरंते धाता देवोजनार्दनः ॥
पिता पितामहो देवस्त्वं मां पालय सर्वदा ॥ 67 ॥ (इति खड्गमन्त्रः ॥)
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्म सर्वायसो ह्यसि ॥
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयोऽहं तव वर्मन्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 68 ॥ ( इति वर्ममन्त्रः ॥) ॥
4.186.m:
Having seen this dark-blue and white [flag], may the enemies of the king perish today,
vanquished in battle by diverse terrible diseases and by weapons!
They became well at once, swept over by your breeze. 63.
Pūtanā, she who is named Revatī, and she who is remembered as Kālarātrī—
resorting to you, O standard, let them quickly consume all enemies! (Thus the standard mantra.)
Asi, the slayer of foes, the sword, fierce in action, hard to approach,
the womb of fortune, victory, and the supporter of righteousness:
these eight names of yours were spoken by the Creator himself.
Your asterism is Kṛttikā, and your venerable deity is Maheśvara.
Gold is your body; your creator is the god Janārdana;
you are the father, the grandfather, the god; protect me always! (Thus the sword mantra.)
You are the giver of comfort in battle, an armour made entirely of iron.
Protect me, for I am to be protected by you, O armour! Reverence to you! (Thus the armour mantra.)

4.186.s:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ .ghoṣāddhṛdayakampan ..
bhava bhūmipa sainyānāṃ tathā vijayavarddhanaḥ .. 69 ..
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyaṃti varavāraṇāḥ ..
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo'smākaṃ mudāvahaḥ ..70..

tathā ca tava śabdena trasyaṃtvasmaddviṣo raṇe..71..( iti duṃdubhimaṃtraḥ ..)

puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṣpāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam ..

śaśāṃkakarasaṃkāśa hima ḍiṃḍīrapāṃḍura ..
protsārayāśu duritaṃ cāmarāmaravallabha .. 74 .. ( iti cāmaramaṃtraḥ ..)
sarvāyudhānāṃ prathamā nirmitā'si pinākinā ..
śūlāyudhādviniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭiparigraham .. 75 ..
4.186.d:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां ।घोषाद्धृदयकम्पन् ॥
भव भूमिप सैन्यानां तथा विजयवर्द्धनः ॥ 69 ॥
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यंति वरवारणाः ॥
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षोऽस्माकं मुदावहः ॥70॥
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासोऽभिजायते ॥
तथा च तव शब्देन त्रस्यंत्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे॥71॥( इति दुंदुभिमंत्रः ॥)
सर्वायुध महामात्र सर्वदेवारिसूदन ॥
चाप मां सर्वदा रक्ष साकं सायकसत्तमैः ॥ 72॥ ( इति चापमन्त्रः॥)
पुण्यस्त्वं शङ्ख पुष्पाणां मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ॥
विष्णुना विधृतो नित्यं मनःशांतिप्रदो भव ॥ 73 ॥ ( इति शङ्खमन्त्रः ॥)
शशांककरसंकाश हिम डिंडीरपांडुर ॥
प्रोत्सारयाशु दुरितं चामरामरवल्लभ ॥ 74 ॥ ( इति चामरमंत्रः ॥)
सर्वायुधानां प्रथमा निर्मिताऽसि पिनाकिना ॥
शूलायुधाद्विनिष्कृष्य कृत्वा मुष्टिपरिग्रहम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.186.m:
O war drum, you cause the hearts of rivals to tremble at your sound!
Become likewise the increaser of victory for the armies of the king!
Just as excellent elephants rejoice at the rumble of a cloud,
so let there be joy bringing delight to us at your sound.
Just as terror arises in women at the sound of a cloud,
so at your sound may our enemies tremble in battle! (Thus the war drum mantra.)
O highest among all weapons, slayer of all enemies of the gods,
O bow, protect me always together with the finest of arrows! (Thus the bow mantra.)
You are holy, O conch, the most auspicious of all auspicious things,
borne constantly by Viṣṇu; become the granter of peace of mind! (Thus the conch mantra.)
Resembling the rays of the moon, white as snow and foam,
quickly drive away misfortune, O chowrie dear to the immortals! (Thus the chowrie mantra.)
First of all weapons you were fashioned by the wielder of Pināka,
drawn forth from the spear-weapon and furnished with a handle.

4.186.m:
You were given to Caṇḍikā, O destroyer of all evil-doers!
Likewise you were multiplied and presented to the gods.
You have become a part of the bodies of all beings, / O dispeller of all inauspiciousness! / O dagger, protect me perpetually and grant peace! Homage to you! 77. (Thus the dagger mantra.)
For driving away evil-doers and for gathering the righteous,
you were also fashioned by Brahmā for the accomplishment of justice.
Give fame, give happiness, be the protector of the king's world;
strike quickly all enemies, O golden sceptre, reverence to you! (Thus the golden sceptre mantra.)
Conquering, granting victory, victorious, slayer of foes, bringing delight,
remover of sorrow, giver of righteousness, tranquil, destroyer of all misfortunes:
because these eight exceedingly strong lions are in your presence,
therefore you are sung by the brahmins in the Vedas as 'throne' [siṃhāsana]!
In you sits Śiva manifest; in you sits Śakra, lord of the gods; / in you sits god Hari; for your sake ascetic penance is performed.

4.186.m:
(Now the prose passage)
Having made according to his means an image of Durgā—golden, silver, brass, wooden, painted, or copper—placed beneath an archway adorned with wood, in a beautiful location, her gaze cast straight ahead, situated in the middle of a decorated chamber, bathed, her limbs anointed with saffron, sandalwood paste, fragrant fourfold unguents, and fine silken garments, having worshipped that goddess with flowers, the king, accompanied by daylight, his fame nurtured by many twice-born folk whose satisfaction has been secured, should himself, along with the family priests, offer worship to the goddess with a bilva leaf and with this mantra:
(Thus the prose is complete)
"Jayaṃtī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī, / Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā, Svadhā, homage be to you!
Born of nectar, the bilva tree is ever dear to the Great Goddess. / I offer a pure bilva leaf to you, O sovereign of the gods!"
And Durgā is to be worshipped from that day with droṇapuṣpī flowers; / and she, the sovereign of the gods, is pleased by that, and the one beset with deep-seated sores [is healed].

4.186.m:
Then, having bowed to the sword that crushes the pride of enemies, / he should desire his own victory, sovereignty, and abundance of food for himself, O king.
Having bowed again and again, he should then meditate in his heart on Śivā, / the slayer of the buffalo, many-armed, the maiden who rides a lion,
threatening the demons, with an upraised sword in her hand, auspicious, / bearing a bell and a rosary, Durgā stationed at the beginning of battle.
Then, with cries of "Victory! Victory!", he should next recite this hymn of praise:
"O you who are the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O Śivā, accomplisher of all aims, / O refuge, three-eyed Gauri, Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you!
Smeared with saffron, anointed with sandalwood paste, / garlanded with bilva leaves, O Durgā, I have come to you for refuge."
Having performed the worship thus, O descendant of Kuru, on the aṣṭamī night [he should keep] a vigil, / and he should have a great festival celebrated with actors, dances, and songs.
Having passed the night thus with joyful folk, at dawn, when the day begins to break, / he should fell buffaloes and sheep before [her], their necks bowed down.

A hundred, or fifty, or half of that, according to his desire; / with jars filled with spirituous liquor he should gratify Parameśvarī.
That should be given to Kāpālikas, and likewise by female and male servants, / distributing it all, O son of Kuntī, among friends, connections, and kinsmen.
Then, in the afternoon on the navamī, the king himself, accompanied by his army, / should conduct Bhavānī seated in a chariot in procession through the realm,
either with thousands of men harnessed to the chariot and well-trained, / very slowly, with blazing lamps of intense brilliance,
and with heroes with drawn swords, with elephants reddened with mineral pigments, / with sounding conches and kettledrums, with dancing courtesans, / with adorned women, and with well-decorated boys.
He should give an offering containing meat to the ghosts with this mantra— / containing blood, containing water, containing cooked food, accompanied by perfume, flowers, and unhusked grain.
Three times each with a trident he should cast the offering in the cardinal and intermediate directions: / "Let the gods, the Ādityas, and likewise the Vasus accept this offering,

नरयानेन वा पार्थ ततोऽविघ्नं समापयेत् ॥1 08॥
अथोत्पन्नेषु विघ्नेषु भूतशांतिं समाचरेत् ॥
येन विघ्ना न जायंते यात्रासंपूर्णतां व्रजेत्॥1 09॥
एवं ये कुर्वते यात्रां राजानोऽन्येऽपि मानवाः॥
महानवम्यां नंदायां पुत्रका हृष्टमानसाः ॥11 0॥
ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यांति भागवतीं पुरीम् ॥1 11॥
4.186.m:
the Maruts, then the two Aśvins, the Rudras, the birds, the serpents, the planets, / the asuras, the yātudhānas, the Mothers, and the piśācas,
the śākinīs, yakṣas, vetālas, yoginīs, pūtanās, jackals, / jṛmbhakas, siddhas, gandharvas, wild beasts, vidyādharas, supporters of the earth,
the guardians of the directions, the world protectors, and those who are obstacle-making vināyakas, / the bringers of peace to the worlds, and Brahmā and the other great seers!
May my sin together with obstacles, and my adversaries, be pacified; / may the ghosts and pretas be gentle, satisfied, and bringers of happiness!"
In this manner he should take goddess Durgā around the realm seated in a chariot, / or in a palanquin, O son of Pṛthā; then he should conclude [the rite] without obstacles.
Now, should obstacles arise, he should perform a pacification of the ghosts, / by which obstacles do not arise and the procession reaches completion.
The kings and other men who conduct the procession in this manner / on Mahānavamī, the Nandā tithi, with joyful minds, O son,
all of them, freed from sin, go to the city of the Divine.

4.186.s:
na teṣāṃ śāvakonāgnirna caurā na vināyakāḥ ..
vighnaṃ kurvanti rājendra yeṣāṃ tuṣṭā maheśvarī .. 112 ..
nīrujaḥ sukhino bhogabhoktāro bhayavarjitāḥ..
bhavaṃti bhaktāḥ puruṣāḥ bhagavatyāḥ kimucyate .. 113 ..
ityeṣa te samākhyāto durgādevyā mahotsavaḥ ..
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvāśubhavināśanaḥ .. 114 ..
śūlāgrabhinnamahiṣāsurapṛṣṭhaviṣṭāmṛtakhātakhaḍgarucirāṃgadabāhudaṇḍām ..
abhyarcya paṃcavadanānugatāṃ navamyāṃ durgāṃ sudurgagahanāni taraṃti martyāḥ .. 115 ..
4.186.d:
न तेषां शावकोनाग्निर्न चौरा न विनायकाः ॥
विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति राजेन्द्र येषां तुष्टा महेश्वरी ॥ 112 ॥
नीरुजः सुखिनो भोगभोक्तारो भयवर्जिताः॥
भवंति भक्ताः पुरुषाः भगवत्याः किमुच्यते ॥ 113 ॥
इत्येष ते समाख्यातो दुर्गादेव्या महोत्सवः ॥
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव सर्वाशुभविनाशनः ॥ 114 ॥
शूलाग्रभिन्नमहिषासुरपृष्ठविष्टामृतखातखड्गरुचिरांगदबाहुदण्डाम् ॥
अभ्यर्च्य पंचवदनानुगतां नवम्यां दुर्गां सुदुर्गगहनानि तरंति मर्त्याः ॥ 115 ॥
4.186.m:
Neither childlessness nor fire, neither thieves nor vināyakas / cause obstacles for those with whom the Great Goddess is pleased, O lord of kings.
Free from disease, happy, enjoyers of pleasures, free from fear / do men who are devoted to the Goddess become; what more need be said?
Thus this great festival of goddess Durgā has been told to you, / destroying all misfortune for those who recite and listen to it.
Having worshipped on the navamī Durgā, who stands upon the back of Mahiṣāsura pierced by the tip of her trident, whose arm-staffs bear bright armlets and a drawn sword, and who is attended by the five-faced [lion], mortals cross over difficult and dense perils.

4.186.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇa uttaraparvaṇi śrīkṛṣṇayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde mahānavamīvratavarṇanaṃ
nāmāṣṭatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..138..
hiraṇyāśvarathadānavidhivarṇanam
4.186.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादे महानवमीव्रतवर्णनं
नामाष्टत्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः॥138॥
हिरण्याश्वरथदानविधिवर्णनम्
4.186.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Mahānavamī Vrata', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa. 138
Description of the rule for the gift of a golden horse-chariot

4.187.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi tava pāṃḍukulodvaha ..
puṇyaṃ hemarathaṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam .. 1 ..
4.187.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि तव पांडुकुलोद्वह ॥
पुण्यं हेमरथं नाम महापातकनाशनम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.187.m: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / Now next, O uplifter of the Pāṇḍu line, I shall proclaim to you / the sacred [gift] named the golden chariot, which destroys great sins.

4.187.s:
puṇye'hni viprakathite svanulipte gṛhāṃgaṇe ..
kṛṣṇājinatilānkṛtvā kāṃcanaṃ sthāpayedratham .. 2 ..
4.187.d:
पुण्येऽह्नि विप्रकथिते स्वनुलिप्ते गृहांगणे ॥
कृष्णाजिनतिलान्कृत्वा कांचनं स्थापयेद्रथम् ॥ 2 ॥
4.187.m: On an auspicious day declared by a Brahmin, in a well-smeared house-courtyard, / having spread a black antelope skin and sesame seeds, he should set up the golden chariot,

4.187.s:
caturasraṃ mahābhāga catuścakraṃ sakūbaram ..
brahmāṇamagrataḥ kṛtvā gṛhītapragrahaṃ śubham .. 3 ..
4.187.d:
चतुरस्रं महाभाग चतुश्चक्रं सकूबरम् ॥
ब्रह्माणमग्रतः कृत्वा गृहीतप्रग्रहं शुभम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.187.m: four-sided, O highly fortunate one, with four wheels and a chariot pole, / having placed Brahmā in front, holding the reins, auspicious,

4.187.s:
iṃdranīlena kuṃbhena dhvajarūpeṇa saṃyutam ..
lokapālāṣṭakopetaṃ padmarāgadalānvitam .. 4 ..
4.187.d:
इंद्रनीलेन कुंभेन ध्वजरूपेण संयुतम् ॥
लोकपालाष्टकोपेतं पद्मरागदलान्वितम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.187.m: endowed with a sapphire jar in the form of a banner, / equipped with the eight world protectors, and furnished with ruby petals,
with four full water-jars and eighteen kinds of grains, / covered with silk cloth, with an awning above.

4.187.s:
madhye tu phalasaṃyuktaṃ puruṣeṇa samanvitam ..
yogayuktaḥ pumānkāryastaṃ ca tatrādhivāsayet .. 6 ..
4.187.d:
मध्ये तु फलसंयुक्तं पुरुषेण समन्वितम् ॥
योगयुक्तः पुमान्कार्यस्तं च तत्राधिवासयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
4.187.m: In the middle, it should be provided with fruit and accompanied by a man; / a man joined in yoga should be made, and one should install him there.

4.187.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ pūjayitvā mālyagaṃdhānulepanaiḥ ..
cakrarakṣāvubhau tasya kāryau viśvakumārakau .. 7 ..
4.187.d:
एवंविधं पूजयित्वा माल्यगंधानुलेपनैः ॥
चक्ररक्षावुभौ तस्य कार्यौ विश्वकुमारकौ ॥ 7 ॥
4.187.m: Having worshipped [a chariot] of such a kind with garlands, fragrant scents, and unguents, / two world-youths should be made as its wheel-protectors.

4.187.s:
puṇyaṃ kālaṃ tataḥ prāpya snātaḥ saṃpūjya devatāḥ ..
triḥpradakṣiṇamāvṛtya gṛhītakusumāṃjaliḥ .. 6 ..
4.187.d:
पुण्यं कालं ततः प्राप्य स्नातः संपूज्य देवताः ॥
त्रिःप्रदक्षिणमावृत्य गृहीतकुसुमांजलिः ॥ 6 ॥
4.187.m: Then, having arrived at an auspicious time, bathed, and worshipped the deities, / circumambulating three times clockwise with an añjali of flowers taken up,
wearing white garlands and white garments, he should utter this mantra:

4.187.s:
namonamaḥ pāpavināśanāya viśvātmane devaturaṃgamāya ..
dhātrāmadhīśāya bhavābhavāya rathasya dānānmama dehi śāṃtim .. 4.187.10 ..
4.187.d:
नमोनमः पापविनाशनाय विश्वात्मने देवतुरंगमाय ॥
धात्रामधीशाय भवाभवाय रथस्य दानान्मम देहि शांतिम् ॥ 4.187.10 ॥
4.187.m: "Homage, homage to the destroyer of sin, the Soul of All, the divine horse! / To the sovereign of creators, to existence and non-existence! Grant me peace through the gift of the chariot!

4.187.s:
vasvaṣṭakādityamarudgaṇānāṃ tvameva dhātā paramaṃ nidhānam ..
yatastato me hṛdayaṃ prayātu dharmaikatānatvamaghaughanāśāt .. 11 ..
4.187.d:
वस्वष्टकादित्यमरुद्गणानां त्वमेव धाता परमं निधानम् ॥
यतस्ततो मे हृदयं प्रयातु धर्मैकतानत्वमघौघनाशात् ॥ 11 ॥
4.187.m: You alone are the creator, the supreme treasury of the eight Vasus, the Ādityas, and the hosts of Maruts! / Therefore, may my heart attain undivided dedication to dharma through the destruction of the flood of sins!"

4.187.s:
iti turagarathapradānametadbhavabhayasūdanamaṃtraṃ yaḥ karoti ..
sakaluṣapaṭalairvimuktadehaḥ paramamupaiti padaṃ pinākapāṇeḥ .. 12 ..
4.187.d:
इति तुरगरथप्रदानमेतद्भवभयसूदनमंत्रं यः करोति ॥
सकलुषपटलैर्विमुक्तदेहः परममुपैति पदं पिनाकपाणेः ॥ 12 ॥
4.187.m: He who performs this gift of a horse-drawn chariot with this mantra that destroys fear of worldly existence, / his body freed from coverings of taint, attains the supreme abode of the Pināka-wielder.

4.187.s:
dedīpyamānavapuṣā ca jitaprabhāvamākramya maḍalamakhaṃḍalacaṃḍabhānoḥ ..
siddhāṃganānayanayugmaprani pīyamānavaktrāṃbujeṃ'bujabhavena ciraṃ sahāste .. 13 ..
4.187.d:
देदीप्यमानवपुषा च जितप्रभावमाक्रम्य मडलमखंडलचंडभानोः ॥
सिद्धांगनानयनयुग्मप्रनि पीयमानवक्त्रांबुजेंऽबुजभवेन चिरं सहास्ते ॥ 13 ॥
4.187.m: With a blazing form, having transcended the power [of death] and traversed the sphere of the unimpaired, fierce-rayed sun, / his lotus-face continuously drunk in by the pair of eyes of wives of the Siddhas, he dwells long with the Lotus-born [Brahmā].

4.187.s:
iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya etatkanakaturaṃgarathapradānamasmin ..
na sa narakapuraṃ vrajetkadācinnarakariporbhavanaṃ prayāti bhūyaḥ .. 14 .. ..
kṛṣṇājinadānavidhivarṇanam
4.187.d:
इति पठति शृणोति वा य एतत्कनकतुरंगरथप्रदानमस्मिन् ॥
न स नरकपुरं व्रजेत्कदाचिन्नरकरिपोर्भवनं प्रयाति भूयः ॥ 14 ॥ ॥
कृष्णाजिनदानविधिवर्णनम्
4.187.m:
Whoever reads or hears of this gift of a golden horse-drawn chariot in this world, / he shall never go to the city of hell; he goes repeatedly to the dwelling of the enemy of Naraka.
Description of the Rite of Giving a Black Antelope Skin

4.188.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
kṛṣṇājinapradānasya vidhikālaṃ mamānagha ..
brāhmaṇaṃ ca samācakṣva tatra me saṃśayo mahān .. 1 ..
4.188.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
कृष्णाजिनप्रदानस्य विधिकालं ममानघ ॥
ब्राह्मणं च समाचक्ष्व तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥ 1 ॥
4.188.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Explain to me, sinless one, the proper time and the recipient Brahmin for the gift of a black antelope skin; / regarding that, I have great doubt.

4.188.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
yugādiṣūparāgeṣu saṃkrāṃtau dinasaṃkṣaye ..
māghyāṃ vā grahapīḍāsu duḥsvapnādbhutadarśane .. 2 ..
4.188.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
युगादिषूपरागेषु संक्रांतौ दिनसंक्षये ॥
माघ्यां वा ग्रहपीडासु दुःस्वप्नाद्भुतदर्शने ॥ 2 ॥
4.188.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / At the beginnings of yugas, during eclipses, at a solstitial or equinoctial transit, on the day of new moon, / or at the full moon of Māgha, during afflictions by planets, or on the sight of bad dreams or portents,

4.188.s:
deyametanmahādānaṃ dravyamātrāgame tathā ..
āhitāgnirdvijo yaśca vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ .. 3 ..
4.188.d:
देयमेतन्महादानं द्रव्यमात्रागमे तथा ॥
आहिताग्निर्द्विजो यश्च वेदवेदांगपारगः ॥ 3 ॥
4.188.m: this great gift should be given, as also upon the arrival of mere wealth. / And to a twice-born who has established the sacred fires, who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

4.188.s:
purāṇābhirato dakṣo deyaṃ tasmai ca pārthiva ..
yathā yena vidhānena tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu .. 4 ..
4.188.d:
पुराणाभिरतो दक्षो देयं तस्मै च पार्थिव ॥
यथा येन विधानेन तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥ 4 ॥
4.188.m: delighting in the Purāṇas, capable—to such a one it should be given, O king. / How and by what rule, hear that from me as I explain it.

4.188.s:
gomayenopalipte tu śucau deśe narādhipa ..
ādāveva samāstīrya śobhitaṃ vastramāvikam .. 5 ..
4.188.d:
गोमयेनोपलिप्ते तु शुचौ देशे नराधिप ॥
आदावेव समास्तीर्य शोभितं वस्त्रमाविकम् ॥ 5 ॥
4.188.m: In a pure place smeared with cow dung, O king, / first having spread out a beautiful woolen cloth,

4.188.s:
kartavyaṃ rukmaśṛṃgaṃ tadraupyadaṃtaṃ tathaiva ca ..
muktādāmnā tu lāṃgūlaṃ tilacchannaṃ tathaiva ca .. 6 ..
4.188.d:
कर्तव्यं रुक्मशृंगं तद्रौप्यदंतं तथैव च ॥
मुक्तादाम्ना तु लांगूलं तिलच्छन्नं तथैव च ॥ 6 ॥
4.188.m: it should be made with golden horns, and likewise with silver teeth, / with a tail adorned by a string of pearls, and covered with sesame seeds.

4.188.s:
tilaiḥ kṛtvā śiro rājanvāsasācchādayedbudhaḥ ..
suvarṇenābhitaḥ kuryādalaṃkuryādviśeṣataḥ .. 7 ..
4.188.d:
तिलैः कृत्वा शिरो राजन्वाससाच्छादयेद्बुधः ॥
सुवर्णेनाभितः कुर्यादलंकुर्याद्विशेषतः ॥ 7 ॥
4.188.m: Having fashioned the head out of sesame seeds, O king, the wise man should cover it with cloth; / he should encircle it with gold and adorn it especially.

4.188.s:
puṣpairgaṃdhaiḥ phalaiścaiva naivedyena ca pūjayet ..
ratnairevaṃ yathāśaktyā tasya dikṣu ca vinyaset .... .. 8 ..
4.188.d:
पुष्पैर्गंधैः फलैश्चैव नैवेद्येन च पूजयेत् ॥
रत्नैरेवं यथाशक्त्या तस्य दिक्षु च विन्यसेत् ॥॥ ॥ 8 ॥
4.188.m: He should worship it with flowers, fragrances, fruits, and food offerings; / likewise, according to his means, he should place jewels in its cardinal directions.

4.188.s:
kāṃsyapātrāṇi catvāri teṣu dadyādyathākramam ..
ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi kṣaudramevaṃ dattvā yathāvidhi .. 9 ..
4.188.d:
कांस्यपात्राणि चत्वारि तेषु दद्याद्यथाक्रमम् ॥
घृतं क्षीरं दधि क्षौद्रमेवं दत्त्वा यथाविधि ॥ 9 ॥
4.188.m: There should be four bronze vessels, and into them he should present in order: / clarified butter, milk, curd, and honey; having given these according to rule,

4.188.s:
tataḥ sarvasamīpe tu maṃtrametamudīrayet ..
kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇamalo deva kṛṣṇājinavarastathā .. 4.188.10 ..
4.188.d:
ततः सर्वसमीपे तु मंत्रमेतमुदीरयेत् ॥
कृष्णः कृष्णमलो देव कृष्णाजिनवरस्तथा ॥ 4.188.10 ॥
4.188.m: then, in the presence of all, he should utter this mantra: / "Kṛṣṇa, O god whose blemish is blackness, and supreme black antelope skin,

4.188.s:
tvaddānāpāstapāpasya prīyatāṃ me namonamaḥ ..
trayastriṃśatsurāṇāṃ ca ādhāre tvaṃ vyavasthitaḥ .. 11 ..
4.188.d:
त्वद्दानापास्तपापस्य प्रीयतां मे नमोनमः ॥
त्रयस्त्रिंशत्सुराणां च आधारे त्वं व्यवस्थितः ॥ 11 ॥
4.188.m: be pleased with me whose sins are dispelled through giving you! Homage, homage! / You stand as the support of the thirty-three deities!

4.188.s:
kṛṣṇo'si mūrtimānsākṣātkṛṣṇājina namo'stu te ..
evaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇipatya punaḥ punaḥ .. 12 ..
4.188.d:
कृष्णोऽसि मूर्तिमान्साक्षात्कृष्णाजिन नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
एवं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य प्रणिपत्य पुनः पुनः ॥ 12 ॥
4.188.m: You are Kṛṣṇa visibly embodied; O black antelope skin, homage be to you!" / Having thus circumambulated it clockwise and bowed down again and again,

4.188.s:
tatpratigrāhakaṃ vipraṃ vedavedāṃgapāragam ..
snātaṃ vastrayugācchannaṃ svaśaktyā vāpyalaṃkṛtam .. 13 ..
4.188.d:
तत्प्रतिग्राहकं विप्रं वेदवेदांगपारगम् ॥
स्नातं वस्त्रयुगाच्छन्नं स्वशक्त्या वाप्यलंकृतम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.188.m: to that recipient Brahmin who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / who has bathed, is clad in a pair of garments, or is adorned according to one's means,

4.188.s:
pratigrahaśca tasyoktaḥ puccha deśe svayaṃbhuvā ..
pratigrahapradagdhasya viprasya ca sa bhārata .. 14 ..
4.188.d:
प्रतिग्रहश्च तस्योक्तः पुच्छ देशे स्वयंभुवा ॥
प्रतिग्रहप्रदग्धस्य विप्रस्य च स भारत ॥ 14 ॥
4.188.m: the acceptance of it was declared at the tail by the Self-born. / And for the Brahmin who is burned by accepting gifts, O Bhārata,

4.188.s:
na paśyedvadanaṃ paścānna cainamabhibhāṣayet ..
anena vidhinā dattvā yathāvatkṛṣṇamārgaṇam .. 15 ..
4.188.d:
न पश्येद्वदनं पश्चान्न चैनमभिभाषयेत् ॥
अनेन विधिना दत्त्वा यथावत्कृष्णमार्गणम् ॥ 15 ॥
4.188.m: one should not look at his face afterwards, nor should one speak to him. / Having given the black antelope skin in this manner according to rule,

4.188.s:
samagraṃ bhūmidānasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ ..
kṛṣṇājinatilānkṛtvā hiraṇyaṃ madhusarpiṣī .. 16 ..
4.188.d:
समग्रं भूमिदानस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
कृष्णाजिनतिलान्कृत्वा हिरण्यं मधुसर्पिषी ॥ 16 ॥
4.188.m: a person obtains the complete fruit of the gift of land. / Having prepared the black antelope skin, sesame seeds, gold, honey, and clarified butter,

4.188.s:
ye prayacchaṃti viprāya na te śocyā bhavaṃti vai ..
sarvām̐llokāṃścaraṃtyeva kāmacārā viyadgatāḥ .. 17 ..
4.188.d:
ये प्रयच्छंति विप्राय न ते शोच्या भवंति वै ॥
सर्वाम्̐ल्लोकांश्चरंत्येव कामचारा वियद्गताः ॥ 17 ॥
4.188.m: those who present them to a Brahmin are indeed not to be pitied; / roaming through the sky at will, they traverse all the worlds.

4.188.s:
ābhūtasaṃplavaṃ yāvatsvargaṃ prāptā na saṃśayaḥ ..
kṛṣṇājinasamaṃ dānaṃ na cāsti bhuvanatraye .. 18 ..
4.188.d:
आभूतसंप्लवं यावत्स्वर्गं प्राप्ता न संशयः ॥
कृष्णाजिनसमं दानं न चास्ति भुवनत्रये ॥ 18 ॥
4.188.m: They have attained heaven until the universal dissolution; of this there is no doubt. / There is no gift equal to a black antelope skin in the three worlds.

4.188.s:
pratigrahopi pāpīyāniti vedavido viduḥ ..
avasthātritaye yacca tridhā yatsamupārjitam .. 19 ..
4.188.d:
प्रतिग्रहोपि पापीयानिति वेदविदो विदुः ॥
अवस्थात्रितये यच्च त्रिधा यत्समुपार्जितम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.188.m: "Accepting a gift is worse [in sin]," thus know the knowers of the Veda. / Whatever has been acquired in the three states [of life] and in three ways,

4.188.s: tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti dattvā kṛṣṇājinaṃ kṣaṇāt .. 4.188.20 ..
4.188.d: तत्सर्वं नाशमायाति दत्त्वा कृष्णाजिनं क्षणात् ॥ 4.188.20 ॥
4.188.m: all that goes to destruction in an instant upon giving a black antelope skin.

4.188.s:
kṛṣṇekṣaṇaṃ kṛṣṇamṛgasya carma dattvā dvijedrāya samāhitātmā ..
yathoktametanmaraṇaṃ na śocetprāpnotyabhīṣṭaṃ manasaḥ phalaṃ yat .. 21 .. ..
hemahastidānavidhivarṇanam
4.188.d:
कृष्णेक्षणं कृष्णमृगस्य चर्म दत्त्वा द्विजेद्राय समाहितात्मा ॥
यथोक्तमेतन्मरणं न शोचेत्प्राप्नोत्यभीष्टं मनसः फलं यत् ॥ 21 ॥ ॥
हेमहस्तिदानविधिवर्णनम्
4.188.m:
Having given the skin of a black antelope, black-eyed, to an eminent twice-born with concentrated mind / as prescribed, he does not grieve over death; he attains whatever desired fruit of his mind [he seeks].
Description of the Rite of Giving a Golden Elephant

4.189.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
kathayiṣye mahārāja hemahastirathaṃ tava ..
yasya pradānādbhavanaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ yāti mānavaḥ .. 1 ..
4.189.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
कथयिष्ये महाराज हेमहस्तिरथं तव ॥
यस्य प्रदानाद्भवनं वैष्णवं याति मानवः ॥ 1 ॥
4.189.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / I will tell you, great king, of the golden-elephant chariot, / by the giving of which a person goes to the realm of Viṣṇu.

4.189.s:
parvakālaṃ samāsādya saṃkrāṃtau grahaṇe'pi vā ..
kuryāddevarathākāraṃ rathaṃ maṇivibhūṣitam .. 2 ..
4.189.d:
पर्वकालं समासाद्य संक्रांतौ ग्रहणेऽपि वा ॥
कुर्याद्देवरथाकारं रथं मणिविभूषितम् ॥ 2 ॥
4.189.m: Having reached an auspicious festival time, at a solstitial or equinoctial transit, or even an eclipse, / one should make a chariot in the shape of a chariot of the gods, adorned with jewels,
with variegated cupolas, equipped with four wheels, / harnessed to four golden elephants, adorned with gold.

4.189.s:
dhvaje ca garuḍaṃ kuryātkūbarāgre vināyakam ..
lokapālāṣṭakopetaṃ brahmārkaśivasaṃyutam .. 4 ..
4.189.d:
ध्वजे च गरुडं कुर्यात्कूबराग्रे विनायकम् ॥
लोकपालाष्टकोपेतं ब्रह्मार्कशिवसंयुतम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.189.m: On the banner he should place Garuḍa, and at the tip of the pole Vināyaka; / it should be equipped with the eight world protectors, and accompanied by Brahmā, the Sun, and Śiva;

4.189.s:
madhye nārāyaṇopetaṃ lakṣmīpuṣṭisamanvitam ..
kṛṣṇājinatiladroṇaṃ kṛtvā taṃ sthāpayedratham .. 5 ..
4.189.d:
मध्ये नारायणोपेतं लक्ष्मीपुष्टिसमन्वितम् ॥
कृष्णाजिनतिलद्रोणं कृत्वा तं स्थापयेद्रथम् ॥ 5 ॥
4.189.m: accompanied in the center by Nārāyaṇa with Lakṣmī and Puṣṭi. / Having placed a droṇa of sesame seeds upon a black antelope skin, he should set down that chariot,
provided with various fruits, with a canopy above, / covered with silk cloth, and worshipped with unfading flowers.

4.189.s:
kuryātpaṃcapalādūrdhvamāśatācca narottama ..
tataḥ snātvā samabhyarcya pitṝndevānyathāvidhi .. 7 ..
4.189.d:
कुर्यात्पंचपलादूर्ध्वमाशताच्च नरोत्तम ॥
ततः स्नात्वा समभ्यर्च्य पितॄन्देवान्यथाविधि ॥ 7 ॥
4.189.m: One should make it from above five palas up to a hundred [palas in weight], O best of men. / Then, having bathed and worshipped the ancestors and gods according to rule,
having circumambulated three times clockwise, taking up an añjali of flowers, / he should utter this mantra, which grants all happiness:

4.189.s:
namonamaḥ śaṃkarapadmajārkalokeśavidyādharavāsudevaiḥ ..
tvaṃ sevyase vedapurāṇayajñaistejo hi naḥ syaṃdana pāhi tasmāt .. 9 ..
4.189.d:
नमोनमः शंकरपद्मजार्कलोकेशविद्याधरवासुदेवैः ॥
त्वं सेव्यसे वेदपुराणयज्ञैस्तेजो हि नः स्यंदन पाहि तस्मात् ॥ 9 ॥
4.189.m: "Homage, homage! You are served by Śaṅkara, the Lotus-born, the Sun, the guardians of the world, Vidyādharas, and Vāsudeva, / and by the Vedas, Purāṇas, and sacrifices; for you are our splendour, O chariot; protect us therefore!"

4.189.s:
yattatpadaṃ paramaguhyatamaṃ purāṇamānaṃdahetugaṇarūpavimuktabandhāḥ ..
yogaikamānasadṛśo munayaḥ samādhau paśyaṃti tattvamasi nātha ratheti rūḍhaḥ .. 4.189.10 ..
4.189.d:
यत्तत्पदं परमगुह्यतमं पुराणमानंदहेतुगणरूपविमुक्तबन्धाः ॥
योगैकमानसदृशो मुनयः समाधौ पश्यंति तत्त्वमसि नाथ रथेति रूढः ॥ 4.189.10 ॥
4.189.m: That ancient, most secret state, free of bonds, whose nature is the cause of bliss, / which sages whose vision is the mind alone in yoga perceive in absorption, that You are, O Lord, manifest as the chariot.

4.189.s:
yasmāttvameva bhavasāgarasaṃplutānāmānaṃdabhāṃḍacitamadhyagapānapātram ..
tasmādaghaughaśamanena kuru prasādaṃ cāmīkarebharatha mādhava saṃpradānāt .. 11 ..
4.189.d:
यस्मात्त्वमेव भवसागरसंप्लुतानामानंदभांडचितमध्यगपानपात्रम् ॥
तस्मादघौघशमनेन कुरु प्रसादं चामीकरेभरथ माधव संप्रदानात् ॥ 11 ॥
4.189.m: Because You alone are the drinking vessel in the midst of the heap of vessels of bliss for those plunged in the ocean of existence, / therefore, by pacifying the flood of sins, show grace, O Mādhava, through the gift of the golden elephant-chariot.

4.189.s:
itthaṃ praṇamya kanakebharathapradānaṃ yaḥ kārayetsakalapāpavimuktadehaḥ ..
vidyādharāmaramunīṃdragaṇābhijuṣṭaṃ prāpnotyasau padamatīṃdriyamiṃdumauleḥ .. 12 ..
4.189.d:
इत्थं प्रणम्य कनकेभरथप्रदानं यः कारयेत्सकलपापविमुक्तदेहः ॥
विद्याधरामरमुनींद्रगणाभिजुष्टं प्राप्नोत्यसौ पदमतींद्रियमिंदुमौलेः ॥ 12 ॥
4.189.m: Having thus bowed down, he who arranges the gift of the golden elephant-chariot, his body freed from all sins, / attains that state of the moon-crested [Śiva] beyond the senses, frequented by hosts of vidyādharas, gods, and sovereign sages.

4.189.s:
kṛtaduritavitānātuṣṭisadvahnipālavyatikarakṛtadehodvegabhāno'pi baṃdhūn..
nayati ca pitṛpautrānrauravādapyaśeṣātkṛtagajarathadānaḥ śāśvataṃ sadma viṣṇoḥ .. 13 .. ..
viśvacakradānavidhivarṇanam
4.189.d:
कृतदुरितवितानातुष्टिसद्वह्निपालव्यतिकरकृतदेहोद्वेगभानोऽपि बंधून्॥
नयति च पितृपौत्रान्रौरवादप्यशेषात्कृतगजरथदानः शाश्वतं सद्म विष्णोः ॥ 13 ॥ ॥
विश्वचक्रदानविधिवर्णनम्
4.189.m:
And he who has made the gift of the elephant-chariot leads all his kinsmen, fathers, and grandsons, / even those whose bodies suffered torment from the contact of the righteous guardians of fire displeased by spreads of committed sins, from Raurava to the eternal abode of Viṣṇu.
Description of the Rules for the Gift of the Viśvacakra

4.190.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
punareva pravakṣyāmi dānamatyadbhutaṃ tava ..
viśvacakramiti khyātaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam .. 1 ..
4.190.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पुनरेव प्रवक्ष्यामि दानमत्यद्भुतं तव ॥
विश्वचक्रमिति ख्यातं सर्वपापविनाशनम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.190.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / Once again I shall tell you of a most wondrous gift, / known as the Viśvacakra, which destroys all sins.

4.190.s:
tapanīyasya śuddhasya viśuddhātmātha kārayet ..
śreṣṭhaṃ palasahasreṇa tadardhena tu madhyamam .. ..2..
4.190.d:
तपनीयस्य शुद्धस्य विशुद्धात्माथ कारयेत् ॥
श्रेष्ठं पलसहस्रेण तदर्धेन तु मध्यमम् ॥ ॥2॥
4.190.m: With a purified mind, one should have it fashioned of pure gold: / the best from one thousand palas, and the intermediate from half of that.

4.190.s:
tasyāpyarddhaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ syādviśvacakramudāhṛtam ..
tathā viṃśatpalādūrdhvamaśakto'pi nivedayet .. 3 ..
4.190.d:
तस्याप्यर्द्धं कनिष्ठं स्याद्विश्वचक्रमुदाहृतम् ॥
तथा विंशत्पलादूर्ध्वमशक्तोऽपि निवेदयेत् ॥ 3 ॥
4.190.m: Half of that again would be the smallest Viśvacakra declared; / likewise, even an incapable man may offer one above twenty palas.

4.190.s:
ṣoḍaśāraṃ tataścakraṃ bhramannemyaṣṭakāvṛtam ..
nābhipadmesthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ yogārūḍhaṃ caturbhujam .. 4 ..
4.190.d:
षोडशारं ततश्चक्रं भ्रमन्नेम्यष्टकावृतम् ॥
नाभिपद्मेस्थितं विष्णुं योगारूढं चतुर्भुजम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.190.m: Then, a wheel with sixteen spokes, surrounded by eight revolving rims; / on the lotus of the nave, [one should depict] four-armed Viṣṇu absorbed in yoga,

4.190.s:
śaṃkhacakre'sya pārśvasthe devyaṣṭakasamāvṛtam ..
dvitīyāvaraṇe tadvatpūrvato jalaśāyinam.. 5 ..
4.190.d:
शंखचक्रेऽस्य पार्श्वस्थे देव्यष्टकसमावृतम् ॥
द्वितीयावरणे तद्वत्पूर्वतो जलशायिनम्॥ 5 ॥
4.190.m: his conch and discus beside him, surrounded by eight goddesses; / in the second enclosure, likewise, in the east, the one who reclines upon the waters:

4.190.s:
atrirbhṛgurvaśiṣṭhaśca brahmā kaśyapa eva ca ..
matsyaḥ kūrmo varāhaśca nārasiṃhotha vāmanaḥ ..6..
4.190.d:
अत्रिर्भृगुर्वशिष्ठश्च ब्रह्मा कश्यप एव च ॥
मत्स्यः कूर्मो वराहश्च नारसिंहोथ वामनः ॥6॥
4.190.m: Atri, Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha, Brahmā, and Kaśyapa, / Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Narsiṃha, then Vāmana,

4.190.s:
rāmo rāmaśca kṛṣṇaśca buddhaḥ kalkī ca te daśa ..
tṛtīyāvaraṇe gaurī manubhirvasurbhiryutā .. 7 ..
4.190.d:
रामो रामश्च कृष्णश्च बुद्धः कल्की च ते दश ॥
तृतीयावरणे गौरी मनुभिर्वसुर्भिर्युता ॥ 7 ॥
4.190.m: Rāma, [Paraśu]rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Buddha, and Kalkin—these ten; / in the third enclosure, Gaurī, accompanied by the Manus and the Vasus;

4.190.s:
caturthe dvādaśādityā vedāścatvāra eva ca ..
pañcame pañca bhūtāni rudrāścaikādaśaiva tu ..8..
4.190.d:
चतुर्थे द्वादशादित्या वेदाश्चत्वार एव च ॥
पञ्चमे पञ्च भूतानि रुद्राश्चैकादशैव तु ॥8॥
4.190.m: in the fourth, the twelve Ādityas and the four Vedas; / in the fifth, the five elements and the eleven Rudras;

4.190.s:
lokapālāṣṭakaṃ ṣaṣṭhe diṅmātaṃgāstathaiva ca ..
saptame'strāṇi sarvāṇi maṃgalāni ca kārayet .. 9 ..
4.190.d:
लोकपालाष्टकं षष्ठे दिङ्मातंगास्तथैव च ॥
सप्तमेऽस्त्राणि सर्वाणि मंगलानि च कारयेत् ॥ 9 ॥
4.190.m: in the sixth, the eight world protectors and likewise the elephants of the directions; / in the seventh, one should place all the weapons and auspicious emblems;

4.190.s:
antarāṃtarato devānvinyasedaṣṭame punaḥ ..
daśahastaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā patākātoraṇānvitam .. 4.190.10 ..
4.190.d:
अन्तरांतरतो देवान्विन्यसेदष्टमे पुनः ॥
दशहस्तं ततः कृत्वा पताकातोरणान्वितम् ॥ 4.190.10 ॥
4.190.m: and in the eighth, one should place the gods at intervals. / Then, having constructed a pavilion of ten cubits, / furnished with flags and archways,

4.190.s:
maṃḍapaṃ kuṇḍamekaṃ ca kārayedvastrasaṃyutam ..
caturhastā bhavedvedī madhye tasyāstato nyaset .. 11 ..
4.190.d:
मंडपं कुण्डमेकं च कारयेद्वस्त्रसंयुतम् ॥
चतुर्हस्ता भवेद्वेदी मध्ये तस्यास्ततो न्यसेत् ॥ 11 ॥
4.190.m: and one sacrificial pit, draped with cloth; / in its middle there should be an altar of four cubits, upon which one should then place,

4.190.s:
kṛṣṇājinoparigataṃ viśvacakraṃ vidhānataḥ ..
tathāṣṭādaśadhānyāni rasāśca lavaṇādayaḥ .. 12 ..
4.190.d:
कृष्णाजिनोपरिगतं विश्वचक्रं विधानतः ॥
तथाष्टादशधान्यानि रसाश्च लवणादयः ॥ 12 ॥
4.190.m: in accordance with rule, the Viśvacakra resting upon a black antelope skin; / likewise the eighteen grains and the flavors beginning with salt,

4.190.s:
pūrṇakumbhāṣṭakaṃ tadvadvastramālyavibhūṣitam ..
phalāni dāpayetpārśve pañcavarṇavitānakam .. 13 ..
4.190.d:
पूर्णकुम्भाष्टकं तद्वद्वस्त्रमाल्यविभूषितम् ॥
फलानि दापयेत्पार्श्वे पञ्चवर्णवितानकम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.190.m: similarly eight full jars adorned with garments and garlands. / At the sides one should cause fruits to be placed, and a canopy of five colors.

4.190.s:
adhivāsya tataścakraṃ paścāddhomaṃ samācaret ..
cātuścaraṇikāṃstatra brāhmaṇāṃścaturotha vā ..14..
4.190.d:
अधिवास्य ततश्चक्रं पश्चाद्धोमं समाचरेत् ॥
चातुश्चरणिकांस्तत्र ब्राह्मणांश्चतुरोथ वा ॥14॥
4.190.m: Then, having performed the consecration of the wheel, one should afterwards perform the fire oblation; / four brāhmaṇas proficient in the four stages of life, or four [brāhmaṇas],

4.190.s:
homaṃ kuryurjitātmāno vastrābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ ..
homadravyasamopetāḥ sruksruvaistāmrabhājanaiḥ .. 15 ..
4.190.d:
होमं कुर्युर्जितात्मानो वस्त्राभरणभूषिताः ॥
होमद्रव्यसमोपेताः स्रुक्स्रुवैस्ताम्रभाजनैः ॥ 15 ॥
4.190.m: self-controlled, adorned with garments and ornaments, / equipped with oblational materials, with sruc and sruva ladles and copper vessels, should perform the oblation.

4.190.s:
cakrapratiṣṭhitānāṃ tu surāṇāṃ homa iṣyate ...
talliṃgairjuhuyānmantraiḥ sarvopadravaśāṃtaye .. 16 ..
4.190.d:
चक्रप्रतिष्ठितानां तु सुराणां होम इष्यते ॥।
तल्लिंगैर्जुहुयान्मन्त्रैः सर्वोपद्रवशांतये ॥ 16 ॥
4.190.m: An oblation is prescribed for the gods established upon the wheel; / one should offer oblations with mantras indicating their characteristics for the pacification of all afflictions.

4.190.s:
tato maṃgalaśabdena snātaḥ śuklāṃbaro gṛhī ..
homādhivāsanāṃte tu gṛhītakusumāṃjaliḥ .. 17 ..
4.190.d:
ततो मंगलशब्देन स्नातः शुक्लांबरो गृही ॥
होमाधिवासनांते तु गृहीतकुसुमांजलिः ॥ 17 ॥
4.190.m: Then, bathed and wearing white garments amidst auspicious sounds, the householder, / at the end of the oblation and consecration, holding a handful of flowers,

4.190.s:
imamuccārayanmaṃtraṃ kṛtvā tattriḥpradakṣiṇam ..
namo viśvaṃbharāyeti viśvacakrātmane namaḥ ..
paramānaṃdarūpī tvaṃ pāhi naḥ pāpakardamāt .. 18 ..
4.190.d:
इममुच्चारयन्मंत्रं कृत्वा तत्त्रिःप्रदक्षिणम् ॥
नमो विश्वंभरायेति विश्वचक्रात्मने नमः ॥
परमानंदरूपी त्वं पाहि नः पापकर्दमात् ॥ 18 ॥
4.190.m: and circumambulating it three times, reciting this mantra: / “Obeisance to the Sustainer of the universe! Obeisance to the Self of the Viśvacakra! / You whose nature is supreme bliss, protect us from the mire of sin!

4.190.s:
tejomayamidaṃ yasmātsadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ..
hṛdi tatra guṇātītaṃ viśvacakraṃ namāmyaham .. 19 ..
4.190.d:
तेजोमयमिदं यस्मात्सदा पश्यंति सूरयः॥
हृदि तत्र गुणातीतं विश्वचक्रं नमाम्यहम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.190.m: Because the wise ever see this luminous [wheel] / in their heart, beyond the qualities, I bow to that Viśvacakra.

4.190.s:
vāsudeve sthitaṃ cakraṃ tasya madhye tu mādhavaḥ ..
anyonyādhārarūpeṇa praṇamāmi sthitāviha .. .. 4.190.20 ..
4.190.d:
वासुदेवे स्थितं चक्रं तस्य मध्ये तु माधवः ॥
अन्योन्याधाररूपेण प्रणमामि स्थिताविह ॥ ॥ 4.190.20 ॥
4.190.m: The wheel is situated in Vāsudeva, and in its center is Mādhava; / I bow to the two situated here, mutually serving as each other's support.

4.190.s:
viśvacakramidaṃ yasmātsarvapāpaharaṃ hareḥ ..
